entries.name: Amo hover button
entries.lite_reason: A small inline <video> in a pill; no blur, no WebGL, no fixed background. Lite is moot because the study is excluded.
entries.touch_reason: The clip plays on hover and resets on leave; there is no tap or press equivalent described, so on a phone the button never reveals anything.
entries.when: A pill button that plays a short bundled clip of its label puffing into glossy 3D letters on hover; not for mini-apps: it is amo's trade dress and hover-only.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, third-party trade dress (amo). Two rules broken: trade dress, and hover-reveal (doctrine: hover may enhance, never reveal). The clip itself would have to live in the bundle; the description says you generate your own, so no remote-asset risk in principle, but a Builder copying the study would point at amo's hosted clip. If a Builder wants the idea, an original is a bundled looping video in a .pill that plays on pointerdown/focus with a poster frame under reduced motion; that is a pattern, not a harvest.
entries.description: On amo a small pill button reveals a short video when you hover it, where the word puffs up into glossy 3D letters. The puffy part is only a video, so the button just plays it on hover and resets on leave, which means you can generate your own clip with any AI video model and drop it in.

entries.name: Apple's corners
entries.lite_reason: A superellipse path applied as clip-path; no filters, no compositing cost, resolution independent.
entries.touch_reason: Static shape on a button or card; the live demo's knob is just a control, the effect itself needs no pointer.
entries.when: True superellipse corners for a button or card via clip-path; use where the Air pill radius still shows a kink, one shape per element.
entries.notes: Harvested as arlan/squircle (1.6kb, lite, touch, motion n/a). Canonical slug squircle matches the recorded status. Note clip-path clips box-shadow and focus rings, so the Kit version is for the shape only; the ring must go on a wrapper.
entries.description: A normal rounded corner has a tiny kink where it meets the flat edge. You feel it before you can name it. Apple fixes this with a squircle, a corner that eases in smooth. Here is the real one on a live button you can play with.

entries.name: Arcade pixel
entries.lite_reason: Recorded in exclusions.md as a WebGL study; WebGL is forbidden under lite and the Kit has only one WebGL component (libraries/metal-fx).
entries.touch_reason: Not pointer-driven; the word renders on its own.
entries.when: A word drawn tiny and blown up so each pixel becomes a big square, rendered in WebGL; not for mini-apps, WebGL is non-lite and the study is excluded.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, WebGL (non-lite). Rule broken: lite forbids WebGL; backgrounds and GPU text are non-lite by default. The look itself is cheap to fake as an original if a game-2d title screen wants it: draw the word on a tiny Canvas 2D and upscale with image-rendering: pixelated (or CSS scale on a low-res canvas), which stays lite and DPR 1. That would be a Builder original, not this study.
entries.description: The letters look pixelated, but there is no pixel grid anywhere: the word is just drawn tiny and blown up, so every little pixel becomes a big square.

entries.name: Chromatic glow
entries.lite_reason: Recorded in exclusions.md as a WebGL study (bloom plus per-channel offset is a shader post effect); WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient glow, not pointer-driven.
entries.when: Soft light bloom that splits into colour fringes at the edges, a WebGL post effect; not for mini-apps, WebGL is non-lite and the study is excluded.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, WebGL (non-lite). Rule broken: lite forbids WebGL. A Builder needing a soft chromatic edge on one hero word can layer three text-shadows (or drop-shadow filters) in red, green and blue offset by a pixel or two with a wide blur; that is a two-line original that degrades to a plain glow under pixel theme. The description is one sentence, so renderer is inferred from the recorded exclusion.
entries.description: I wanted light that blooms out soft and pulls the colors apart at the edges.

entries.name: Dia Browser's gradient
entries.lite_reason: A full-width, screen-bottom glow made of heavily blurred colour bars is an animated background with filter: blur over most of the viewport; backgrounds are non-lite unless pure flat gradients, and a fixed bottom glow is a fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Plays once on load; nothing depends on hover or pointer.
entries.when: A bottom-of-screen glow of blurred colour bars that grows up on load; not for mini-apps, it reproduces Dia Browser's identity and is a full-screen background.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, third-party trade dress (Dia Browser). Rule broken: trade dress; secondarily a full-screen blurred background, non-lite. A generic bottom glow in Air tokens (var(--accent) bars, no Dia palette) is already covered in spirit by fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg, which renders flat under lite and pixel theme.
entries.description: Dia Browser has a soft glow at the bottom of the screen. A row of blurry colour bars, short on the sides and tall in the middle, going from dark up through blue, white, yellow, red and pink, then fading out at the top. It grows up from the floor when the page loads.

entries.name: Fade motion
entries.lite_reason: Recorded in exclusions.md as a WebGL study; two hundred additive copies of a glyph is a GPU accumulation trick, and WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous headline motion, not pointer-driven.
entries.when: A headline motion-blurred by stacking hundreds of faint copies on the GPU; not for mini-apps, WebGL is non-lite and the study is excluded.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, WebGL (non-lite). Rule broken: lite forbids WebGL. Do not attempt a DOM port: two hundred stacked text layers per word is a compositing bill the 390px webview cannot pay. If a headline needs a motion-blur entrance, fancy/vertical-cut-reveal or arlan/typer is the Kit answer.
entries.description: Thought this was a blur. It's two hundred copies of the word stacked almost invisibly, and the fade is just where a lot of them piled up.

entries.name: Figma vector editor
entries.lite_reason: Selection box, handles, size tag and bezier points are plain SVG/DOM overlays with no filters.
entries.touch_reason: Dragging handles works with pointer events on touch, but the corner squares and bezier dots are far below the 44px target rule and would need enlarged hit areas.
entries.when: Figma-style selection chrome: thin blue box, corner handles, size tag and draggable bezier points; not for mini-apps, it is Figma's trade dress.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, third-party trade dress (Figma). Rule broken: trade dress. Slug discrepancy: the canonical URL is /vault/vector-editor and the index card is titled 'Figma vector editor', but kit.sources.json and exclusions.md record the study under the slug 'figma'; treat them as the same study. A drag-to-edit shape tool for a 'tool' template would be a Builder original in Air tokens with 44px handles, not this look.
entries.description: You know that Figma look everyone copies: the thin blue box around a thing, the little corner squares, the size tag under it, and the dots you grab to bend a shape. I wanted to see if I could build it for the web, so here it is.

entries.name: Ghosty reveal
entries.lite_reason: A mask-image wipe animated with transform/mask-position; no backdrop-filter, no WebGL, one compositing layer.
entries.touch_reason: Plays on mount or on view; nothing depends on hover or pointer.
entries.when: Mask-image wipe that lets a photo bleed in through a soft cloudy edge; use for one hero image or gallery reveal per screen, mask asset bundled.
entries.notes: Harvested as arlan/ghosty-reveal (1.0kb, lite, touch, motion static). The soft mask image must ship inside the bundle (a small PNG or an inline SVG turbulence mask); a remote mask URL would fail the CSP ceiling. Counts as the screen's hero motion when used on the hero image.
entries.description: I love it when photos do not just fade in. The good ones bleed in through a soft, cloudy edge, like the image is forming out of fog. It looks expensive and hard to build. It is neither.

entries.name: Holo
entries.lite_reason: kit-index records lite=true: gradients, blend modes and a 3D transform on one card, no WebGL and no backdrop-filter. The blend modes are heavy, so one per screen.
entries.touch_reason: Tilt is driven by device orientation or a finger drag as well as the pointer, so the effect exists on a phone without hover.
entries.when: Holographic foil card that tilts with a finger drag or device orientation; use once per screen for a ticket, pass or profile hero.
entries.notes: Harvested as arlan/holo (6.0kb, lite, touch, motion static, 'one per screen; heavy blend modes'). The study frames itself as an Airbnb identity card rebuilt; the Kit component is the generic foil card, so a Builder must not restore Airbnb layout or marks. DeviceOrientation needs a user gesture on iOS; the Kit version falls back to drag.
entries.description: Airbnb's identity card, rebuilt as a holo card for my girlfriend. Tilt it and the foil catches the light, the hearts come up on the side you turned, and her photo flips its colours.

entries.name: Kinetic typography
entries.lite_reason: A grid of tiles each showing a clipped slice of the glyph and translated on a sine wave; transforms only, no filters, no WebGL. A 6x8 grid per letter is a modest layer count at 390px.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous wave loop; nothing depends on hover or pointer position.
entries.when: A hero letter or short word sliced into tiles that ripple on independent sine waves; the single hero motion on a title screen, never body copy.
entries.notes: Kit status: not reviewed for Kit 2026.09. tier-a-harvest-candidate: the source is MIT ('MIT -> free to copy') and could be harvested as @kit/arlan/kinetic-typography at the next harvest; until then a Builder can write an original (N x M overflow-hidden tiles, each holding an offset copy of the glyph in var(--font-body), translateY by sin(t + row + col) via rAF or CSS animation-delay). Must be the screen's one hero motion, finite or aria-hidden, and a plain glyph under reduced motion. Renderer inferred from the description (could equally be Canvas 2D slices), hence medium confidence. Not in this crawl: the three owner-supplied arlan typographic pieces (shutter-type, swing-type, rush-type); they are not among these 18 studies and get no entries here.
entries.description: A letter is cut into a grid of tiles, and each tile slips on its own wave, so the whole letter ripples like water.

entries.name: Liquid UI
entries.lite_reason: SDF plus marching squares produces an SVG path each frame; no filters, no WebGL, one path element behind the cards.
entries.touch_reason: Cards are dragged, which works with pointer events on touch; the join re-flows from card positions, not from hover.
entries.when: SDF-driven liquid silhouettes that fuse neighbouring cards with an inward bend; a decorative group background behind a card cluster, not layout.
entries.notes: Harvested as arlan/liquid-ui (2.9kb, lite, touch, motion static, 'decorative group backgrounds only'). The Kit component is the silhouette engine; the draggable demo cards are the study's playground, not part of the component. libraries/liquid-gooey is the lighter answer when the merge is a menu or tab thumb rather than cards.
entries.description: I love UI where two cards fuse and the corner between them bends inward, like they were poured together, so I built a tiny engine that just makes it from code instead of drawing it by hand. Drag the cards below to watch the join re-flow, and turn one knob to go from crisp joints all the way to soft gooey blobs.

entries.name: Midjourney Medical's ASCII
entries.lite_reason: Real text nodes moved with transforms; no filters, no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Plays on load; nothing depends on hover or pointer.
entries.when: Loose letters spin and settle into a wordmark as live text on load; not for mini-apps, it reproduces the Midjourney Medical identity.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, third-party trade dress (Midjourney). Rule broken: trade dress. The underlying idea (characters converge into a word on load) is covered by fancy/scramble-in for short labels, and a Builder can write a converge-on-mount original for one hero word; the study's value is the Midjourney wordmark choreography, which must not be reproduced.
entries.description: This is the Midjourney Medical page. When it loads, a bunch of letters spin around and slowly form the Midjourney name. The cool part is that it's not a video or an image. It's all real text that the code moves around live.

entries.name: Pixel brushes
entries.lite_reason: Canvas 2D stamping along a path at DPR 1; no filters, no WebGL, cost scales with stamp count only.
entries.touch_reason: Drawing follows the pointer path, which on a phone is the finger; pointer events cover both. The canvas needs touch-action: none so strokes do not scroll the webview.
entries.when: Canvas 2D brush that stamps a small shape along the finger's path, from crisp line to loose spray; use for a doodle, signature or guestbook sketch.
entries.notes: Kit status: not reviewed for Kit 2026.09. Decision: build-original rather than harvest. Stamping a shape every N px along an interpolated pointer path with spacing, size jitter and scatter parameters is a few dozen lines of Canvas 2D; a Builder writes it under the contract without vendored code, so no tier-a-harvest-candidate flag. Contract notes for the Builder: canvas at DPR 1 under lite, touch-action: none, 44px tool controls, and if the drawing must persist store stroke point lists (not bitmaps) behind useAirState within the 256 KiB resource limit; no localStorage. User-driven marks are not animation, so reduced motion is n/a.
entries.description: A brush is a small shape stamped over and over along a path, and a handful of numbers turn the same code into a crisp line or a loose spray.

entries.name: Ransom note
entries.lite_reason: One image per typed letter with a random rotation; no filters, no WebGL. Lite is moot because the imagery cannot ship.
entries.touch_reason: Typing into a field; no hover or pointer dependency.
entries.when: Type with real cut-out magazine letters taped down crooked; not for mini-apps as published, the letter imagery is site-hosted and was never captured.
entries.notes: Kit status: gap, depends on site-hosted cut-out letter imagery and an unpublished manifest that was not captured (recorded in kit.sources.json, never fabricated). Rule broken: needs remote assets; the CSP ceiling forbids any host reference, and bundling a full cut-out alphabet with variants would be several hundred KiB of images. If a Builder wants the mood, an original in Air tokens is possible without imagery: each letter in a tinted chip with random rotate/scale, alternating var(--font-body) and var(--font-ui), which is a style, not this study.
entries.description: I always liked the ransom-note look, where every letter is torn from a different magazine and taped down crooked. So I took a set of real cut-out letters and made it into something you can type with.

entries.name: Realistic emboss
entries.lite_reason: Recorded in exclusions.md as a WebGL study (per-pixel lighting on a height map); WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Static or ambient material rendering, not pointer-driven.
entries.when: Realistic embossed lettering with directional light, rendered in WebGL; not for mini-apps, WebGL is non-lite and the study is excluded.
entries.notes: Kit status: excluded, WebGL (non-lite). Rule broken: lite forbids WebGL. The description is one sentence, so renderer follows the recorded exclusion. An embossed label for a 'page' or 'store' header is a cheap original: two text-shadows (light offset up-left, dark offset down-right) on ink-coloured text, or an inline SVG feDiffuseLighting filter; both are lite and match arlan/color-depth's skeuomorphic buttons.
entries.description: Really liked the emboss effect people do, so I replicated it in web.

entries.name: Symbols effect
entries.lite_reason: The description says it all runs on the GPU so video plays through it live; a full-frame fragment shader over media is WebGL and forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Media drop-in and playback; nothing depends on hover or pointer. On a phone the drop zone becomes a file input.
entries.when: GPU filter that cuts an image or live video into four brightness bands stamped with tinted symbols; not for mini-apps, GPU-only makes it non-lite.
entries.notes: Kit status: not reviewed for Kit 2026.09. Decision: not-for-miniapp, WebGL/GPU makes it non-lite and the study's point is live video through the shader, which lite cannot serve and reduced motion would have to freeze to a poster. Slug discrepancy: the canonical URL is /vault/sandbox, the index card is titled 'Symbols effect', and kit.sources.json records it as 'sandbox (Symbols effect; index slug symbols)'; treat all three as this one study. A still-image variant (four brightness bands posterised and stamped with glyphs on Canvas 2D at DPR 1) would be a Builder original for a gallery hero, not a harvest of this GPU code. Any bundled media must be in-bundle; no remote video.
entries.description: Drop in an image or a video and it gets cut into four brightness bands. Each band is stamped with a tiny symbol, tinted with its own colour, so the picture is rebuilt out of little marks. It all runs on the GPU, so video plays through it live.

entries.name: The art of color depth
entries.lite_reason: Layered gradients, inset shadows and borders as pure CSS classes; no backdrop-filter, no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Static materials on buttons; press states work on tap, nothing is hover-only.
entries.when: Ten layered-light CSS materials (glossy, glass, metal, cushion) for buttons; use on the one primary action of a screen, never on every control.
entries.notes: Harvested as arlan/color-depth (3.4kb, lite, touch, motion n/a; pure CSS classes, SKILL.md ships as ref). Materials must sit on Air tokens so they read under both atmosphere and pixel themes; the glass material should not add backdrop-filter under lite. Canonical slug color-depth matches the recorded status.
entries.description: Buttons that feel like real objects, glossy glass or brushed metal or a soft cushion. They look expensive and slow to make. They are neither.

entries.name: The typer
entries.lite_reason: Per-letter spans toggling pill, highlight and outline classes with transforms and background; no filters, no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Plays on mount as a headline or status line; nothing depends on hover or pointer.
entries.when: Eased typing where a wave flickers each letter through pill, highlight and outline states before landing; for one headline or status line.
entries.notes: Harvested as arlan/typer (2.7kb, lite, touch, motion static; vanilla class plus React wrapper). Alternative to fancy/typewriter when the out-animation is needed; adjacent letters in the same state merge into one rounded bar, so it needs var(--font-ui) sizing that keeps the bars legible at 390px. Counts as the screen's hero motion. Canonical slug typer matches the recorded status.
entries.description: Most headlines fade in. The nice ones type in. A wave runs across the line, and as it passes each letter the letter flickers through a few states, a solid pill, a highlight, an outlined pill, then lands on plain text. Letters next to each other in the same state merge into one long rounded bar.

entries.name: Animated Content
entries.lite_reason: Transform and opacity transition only; no WebGL, blur or fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Entrance plays on mount; nothing depends on a pointer.
entries.when: A block that fades and slides in from a chosen side on mount; reach for Air's --slide-in for a panel's first paint and never tie the entrance to scroll.
entries.notes: The source is a GSAP + ScrollTrigger wrapper (hence heavy). The mount variant is exactly Air's var(--slide-in) settle motion (<=300ms ease-out). The scroll-triggered variant breaks 'nothing moves on scroll; no scroll-linked reveals' and is dropped. Nothing to vendor.
entries.description: Wrapper that animates any children on scroll or mount with configurable direction, distance, duration, easing and disappear options.

entries.name: Antigravity
entries.lite_reason: 3D particle field rendered in WebGL; lite forbids WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Particles repel from the cursor; on a phone the field is inert until a finger drags, and there is no hover position to repel from.
entries.when: A 3D particle field that scatters away from the mouse cursor; a desktop pointer toy with no finger equivalent and no place inside Messages.
entries.notes: Breaks 'touch first' (cursor-following effect; there is no cursor on touch) and is WebGL, so non-lite. A full-viewport GPU particle background is also the kind of ambient loop doctrine treats as decoration at best. Not worth packing.
entries.description: 3D antigravity particle field that repels from the cursor with smooth motion.

entries.name: Blob Cursor
entries.lite_reason: DOM elements with a goo filter and transforms; no WebGL. Moot, since the effect is cursor-bound.
entries.touch_reason: A cursor replacement that follows the pointer; there is no pointer on touch.
entries.when: A gooey blob that trails the mouse pointer with inertia; there is no pointer on a phone, so it has no use in a mini-app.
entries.notes: Breaks 'touch first': a cursor-following effect with no tap or drag equivalent. If a gooey merge is wanted, libraries/liquid-gooey and fancy/gooey-svg-filter already cover the material.
entries.description: Organic blob cursor that smoothly follows the pointer with inertia and elastic morphing.

entries.name: Click Spark
entries.lite_reason: A few line strokes on a 2D canvas overlay for ~400ms; no WebGL, blur or fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Click maps directly to tap; the burst originates at the touch point.
entries.when: A short burst of sparks where the finger taps; use it once for the confirming tap (RSVP sent, item added), never as ambient decoration.
entries.notes: A dozen lines of Canvas 2D: on pointerdown draw N radial strokes that translate outward and fade. Keep the canvas pointer-events:none over the tap target, cap DPR at 1 under lite, and skip spawning under reduced motion. Counts as the screen's one hero motion if paired with the confirming action.
entries.description: Creates particle spark bursts at click position.

entries.name: Crosshair
entries.lite_reason: Two DOM lines translated with the pointer; no WebGL. Moot, since it is a cursor replacement.
entries.touch_reason: Custom cursor with link-hover reactions; there is no cursor or hover on touch.
entries.when: A custom crosshair cursor that tracks the mouse and reacts to links; replacing the cursor means nothing on touch.
entries.notes: Breaks 'touch first' twice: cursor-following and hover-revealed link states ('hover may enhance but never reveal'). No tap equivalent is described.
entries.description: Custom crosshair cursor with tracking, and link hover effects.

entries.name: Cubes
entries.lite_reason: CSS 3D transforms on a handful of DOM faces; no WebGL, blur or fixed background. Keep the cluster small (<=3x3) so paint stays cheap on a lite surface.
entries.touch_reason: Auto-rotation mode needs no pointer; hover tilt is an enhancement, not the only way in.
entries.when: A small cluster of CSS cubes turning slowly as a hero object; compose it from fancy/css-box, auto-rotating, with hover as an optional extra and never the only input.
entries.notes: Source leans on GSAP for the tilt and stagger; fancy/css-box is already the CSS 3D cube, so the cluster is a small grid of css-box instances sharing one CSS keyframe rotation, which is light. Prefer a single css-box when the faces carry content. Under reduced motion show the cluster at a fixed isometric angle. Ambient loop: mark aria-hidden. Nothing to vendor.
entries.description: 3D rotating cube cluster. Supports auto-rotation or hover interaction.

entries.name: Cursor Grid
entries.lite_reason: 2D canvas grid with per-cell alpha; no WebGL. Cap DPR at 1 under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Click pulses map to tap and a finger drag supplies the pointer position, so cells light under the finger the same way fancy/pixel-trail does; the hover falloff at rest is the only part lost.
entries.when: A canvas grid whose cells glow under the pointer or finger and pulse on tap; the Kit's pixel-trail already does this, so use that.
entries.notes: fancy/pixel-trail is the touch-native rendition of the same idea (pixels light under pointer or finger, decorative background for one screen). The hover-radius falloff is the only part pixel-trail lacks and it has no meaning without a hovering cursor. Nothing to vendor.
entries.description: Canvas grid whose cells light up around the cursor with configurable radius, falloff and click pulses.

entries.name: Elastic Mesh
entries.lite_reason: Per-frame spring physics across a full mesh; the Kit marks physics components non-lite (see fancy/elastic-line), and the surface may be GPU-drawn.
entries.touch_reason: The mesh stretches under a hovering pointer; a finger can drag it, but the surface is inert at rest and the effect is a hover toy.
entries.when: A full-surface spring mesh that stretches under the pointer and settles; a hover physics playground, inert under a thumb and too heavy for a card.
entries.notes: Breaks 'touch first' (pointer-driven) and falls under 'giant full-page physics playgrounds'. fancy/elastic-line is the contained, single-divider version already in the Kit if a spring flourish is wanted. Renderer is inferred; the source may use WebGL, which would only strengthen the exclusion.
entries.description: Spring-mesh surface that stretches under the pointer and settles back with damped physics.

entries.name: Electric Border
entries.lite_reason: SVG turbulence/displacement filter on a border plus a CSS glow; no WebGL or backdrop-filter. Under lite render a steady static glow instead of the animated filter.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient border loop; nothing depends on a pointer.
entries.when: A crackling electric outline around one card; use it for the single live or pending item and fall back to a steady glow under lite or reduced motion.
entries.notes: An original is an inline SVG filter (feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap, seed animated on a short loop) applied to a border layer, with a box-shadow glow in var(--accent). Animated displacement filters are paint-heavy on phones, so freeze the seed under lite and reduced motion. Same job as libraries/border-beam (one card that deserves attention); pick one per screen.
entries.description: Jittery electric energy border with animated arcs, glow and adjustable intensity.

entries.name: Fade Content
entries.lite_reason: Opacity and transform transition; no WebGL, blur or fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Entrance plays when the block enters view; nothing depends on a pointer.
entries.when: A block that fades or slides in once it scrolls into view; nothing reveals on scroll inside Messages, so use Air's --slide-in on mount instead.
entries.notes: Breaks 'nothing moves on scroll; no scroll-linked reveals': the only trigger described is threshold-based (IntersectionObserver) activation, with no mount variant, so unlike animated-content there is no exception. The mount-time fade/slide a screen actually needs is Air's var(--slide-in) settle motion (<=300ms ease-out). Nothing to vendor.
entries.description: Simple directional fade / slide entrance / exit wrapper with threshold-based activation.

entries.name: Ghost Cursor
entries.lite_reason: Shader-drawn trail in WebGL; lite forbids WebGL. Moot, since it is cursor-bound.
entries.touch_reason: Follows the real cursor; there is no cursor on touch.
entries.when: A translucent trail that follows the mouse cursor; cursor followers do not exist on touch and are out of scope for a mini-app.
entries.notes: Breaks 'touch first' (cursor-following effect) and is WebGL, so non-lite. Renderer inferred from the smoky trail look; even as DOM it would be excluded.
entries.description: Semi-transparent ghost cursor that smoothly follows the real cursor with a trailing effect.

entries.name: Glare Hover
entries.lite_reason: A translated linear-gradient overlay with overflow hidden; no WebGL, blur or fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Glare sweeps on hover only; no tap or press trigger is described.
entries.when: A light glare sweeping across a card on hover; rebuild it as a one-shot CSS sweep on press or on mount, since hover never reveals on touch.
entries.notes: Ten lines of CSS: a pseudo-element gradient translated across the card on :active or once on mount. Hover may keep it as an enhancement. arlan/holo already covers the pointer/device-orientation foil version with real glare; this is the cheaper flat sweep.
entries.description: Adds a realistic moving glare highlight on hover over any element.

entries.name: Glow Cursor
entries.lite_reason: Shader-powered light trail; lite forbids WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Follows the pointer; there is no pointer on touch.
entries.when: A shader light trail drawn behind the mouse pointer; WebGL, cursor-bound and non-lite, so it is not for a mini-app.
entries.notes: Breaks 'touch first' (cursor-following effect) and is WebGL, so non-lite. Described as shader-powered, so the renderer is certain.
entries.description: Shader-powered light trail that smoothly follows the pointer with customizable glow, color, taper and pulse.

entries.name: Gradual Blur
entries.lite_reason: The source stacks backdrop-filter layers to build the gradient blur, which lite forbids; the rebuilt version uses a plain filter on the element and passes lite.
entries.touch_reason: Driven by scroll position or a trigger, not by pointer position.
entries.when: Content that un-blurs from soft to sharp on a trigger. Build it as a one-shot mount reveal (filter: blur to 0 in 300ms), never scroll-driven; sharp from the start under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Only the trigger mode is usable: the scroll mode breaks 'nothing moves on scroll inside the webview' and the source's stacked backdrop-filter layers break lite, and it pulls mathjs for easing. Rebuild as an element filter: blur(12px) to 0 over 300ms on mount or tap (filter, not backdrop-filter, so it passes lite); counts as the screen's hero motion; cut to sharp under reduced motion.
entries.description: Progressively un-blurs content based on scroll or trigger creating a cinematic reveal.

entries.name: Halftone Reveal
entries.lite_reason: Per-pixel dot field over an image redrawn every frame across the whole surface; reads as a GPU effect and is non-lite either way.
entries.touch_reason: Content sharpens only around the cursor; no tap or drag equivalent is described.
entries.when: Halftone dot screen over an image that sharpens where the pointer is. Not used: a hover-revealed image is a hover-only affordance and there is no cursor in Messages.
entries.notes: Breaks 'hover may enhance but never reveal' and 'no cursor on touch'. Renderer is inferred (per-pixel sampling suggests a shader). If a print texture is wanted, a static CSS radial-gradient dot pattern or an SVG filter over the image does it under lite.
entries.description: Print-style halftone dot matrix that resolves into sharp content around the cursor.

entries.name: Image Trail
entries.lite_reason: Absolutely positioned images moved with transform and opacity; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Spawns images along the cursor path; a finger drag would hide the trail under the hand.
entries.when: Images that spawn and fade along the pointer's path. Not used: cursor-following decoration has no meaning on a 390px touch card; show photos with fancy/simple-carousel.
entries.notes: Breaks 'no cursor on touch' and needs gsap. Any images would have to ship in the bundle. The gallery recipe (fancy/simple-carousel) is the Kit's way to show a set of photos.
entries.description: Cursor-based image trail with several built-in variants.

entries.name: Laser Flow
entries.lite_reason: Three.js fragment-shader scene with volumetric fog; WebGL is off under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The beam animates on its own; pointer position only tilts it as an enhancement.
entries.when: A laser beam that pours light onto a surface behind a hero title. One per screen as the hero motion of a launch or game landing; a flat gradient plate under lite and reduced motion.
entries.notes: A shader scene that cannot be rebuilt in CSS, so it qualifies for the restricted allowlist next to Beams and Light Rays. It must render a static gradient frame when WebGL, lite or reduced motion says no. It overlaps Light Rays and Side Rays; pack only if the beam-on-surface look is asked for.
entries.description: Dynamic laser light that flows onto a surface, customizable effect.

entries.name: Logo Loop
entries.lite_reason: A translated strip of inline images; no filters, blur or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous loop; hover pause only enhances and is not required.
entries.when: Endless strip of logos with seamless repeat and pause on hover. Already covered by fancy/simple-marquee, which takes logos, photos or words and pauses under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Logos must ship in the bundle; no CDN icon packs. fancy/simple-marquee is the Kit's marquee and already handles the seamless repeat. Nothing to add.
entries.description: Continuously looping marquee of brand or tech logos with seamless repeat and hover pause.

entries.name: Magic Rings
entries.lite_reason: The glowing ring field reads as a GPU effect; WebGL is off under lite.
entries.touch_reason: 'Interactive' means the rings follow pointer position; no tap equivalent is described.
entries.when: Concentric glowing rings that ripple as the pointer moves. Build it: a few SVG circles with a stroke pulse fired by a tap; rings sit still under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Vague description and the renderer is inferred. A ring pulse is well within CSS/SVG (transform: scale plus opacity, settling in 300ms) and needs no vendored code; make the interaction tap-driven because there is no cursor. Not for status; libraries/thinking-orbs and aicss/orbs own the agent-presence read.
entries.description: Interactive magic rings effect with customizable parameters.

entries.name: Magnet
entries.lite_reason: A transform on one element; nothing heavy.
entries.touch_reason: Eases toward the cursor; on touch the finger is already on the target so there is nothing to attract.
entries.when: A button that leans toward the cursor and springs back. Not used: there is no cursor in Messages; a 44px target with a press state is the touch affordance.
entries.notes: Breaks 'no cursor on touch'. Give Air .row.actions buttons a press-scale (transform: scale(.97), 150ms ease-out) instead.
entries.description: Elements magnetically ease toward the cursor then settle back with spring physics.

entries.name: Magnet Lines
entries.lite_reason: A grid of rotated spans driven by transform; no filters or WebGL, though the node count is high.
entries.touch_reason: Lines aim at the cursor; nothing to aim at on touch and no drag equivalent is described.
entries.when: A grid of short lines that rotate to point at the cursor. Not used: cursor-following decoration with no touch equivalent, and hundreds of nodes for a 390px card.
entries.notes: Breaks 'no cursor on touch'. A touch-drag field would be possible but is not what the source does and would still be a heavy DOM grid. fancy/pixel-trail is the Kit's finger-driven decorative background.
entries.description: Animated field lines bend toward the cursor.

entries.name: Meta Balls
entries.lite_reason: OGL fragment shader computing the implicit surface; WebGL is off under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Blobs drift and merge on their own; the pointer-following ball is optional.
entries.when: Soft blobs that merge and split as they drift. Already covered: arlan/liquid-ui merges card silhouettes and fancy/gooey-svg-filter goos any animated circles, both without WebGL.
entries.notes: arlan/liquid-ui (SDF plus marching squares) gives the implicit-surface read; libraries/liquid-gooey and fancy/gooey-svg-filter give the merging-droplet read. All are lite. Nothing to pack.
entries.description: Liquid metaball blobs that merge and separate with smooth implicit surface animation.

entries.name: Metallic Paint
entries.lite_reason: Custom WebGL shader sampling an SVG mask; WebGL is off under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient shimmer that needs no pointer.
entries.when: Liquid chrome shimmer filling an SVG logo or word. Already covered by libraries/metal-fx, which renders a flat plate when WebGL, lite or reduced motion is off.
entries.notes: Same effect class as libraries/metal-fx, the Kit's one WebGL component. The source expects a rasterized SVG mask; metal-fx wraps a child. Nothing to add.
entries.description: Liquid metallic paint shader which can be applied to SVG elements.

entries.name: Noise
entries.lite_reason: Full-viewport canvas redrawn every frame; an animated full-screen overlay is non-lite. A static grain tile is fine.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient overlay; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Film-grain overlay that gives a flat canvas some texture. Build it: SVG feTurbulence as a static tile at low opacity; animate only in atmosphere and only as aria-hidden decoration.
entries.notes: A continuously redrawn full-screen canvas burns battery inside Messages. Prefer a static feTurbulence data URI or a small tiled canvas texture; if it animates, keep it a finite or aria-hidden loop and static under lite and reduced motion.
entries.description: Animated film grain / noise overlay adding subtle texture and motion.

entries.name: Orbit Images
entries.lite_reason: Images moved along an SVG path with transforms; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous orbit; no pointer needed.
entries.when: Images that travel around a custom SVG path. Already covered: fancy/circling-elements orbits avatars or badges around a center, and fancy/text-along-path handles arbitrary paths.
entries.notes: Images must ship in the bundle. If a non-circular orbit is really wanted, CSS offset-path/offset-distance on circling-elements' items does it without vendored code.
entries.description: SVG Path customizable orbiting images effect.

entries.name: Pixel Swap
entries.lite_reason: The source appears GPU-backed for the pixel dissolve; WebGL is off under lite. The effect itself needs no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Trigger-based (hover, click, timer); a tap trigger works as well as a click.
entries.when: A grid of pixel blocks covers a card, the content swaps underneath, and the blocks dissolve. Build it as a CSS grid with staggered opacity for a tap-to-flip card or a confirmation swap.
entries.notes: Renderer is a guess; the original may be Three-based, but the effect is a DOM grid of squares with staggered transitions settling in 300ms, and it counts as the screen's hero motion if used. Under reduced motion cut straight to the swapped content; fancy/pixelate-svg-filter is the related lite helper for images.
entries.description: Pixel fragments assemble into a full cover, swap arbitrary content, then dissolve away with reversible colors and triggers.

entries.name: Pixel Trail
entries.lite_reason: A Three.js GPGPU shader canvas layered over the whole screen; WebGL is forbidden under lite and the layer animates continuously.
entries.touch_reason: Driven by pointer-move only; the description gives no tap or drag equivalent, and the finger covers the trail it draws.
entries.when: Squares light up and fade behind the pointer for a retro digital feel; use fancy/pixel-trail instead, which does the same under a finger on a 2D canvas and stays lite.
entries.notes: Tier A fancy/pixel-trail already covers this on a 2D canvas with finger input and no Three dependency. The React Bits version is a shader over R3F/drei and non-lite; nothing to pack. Like the Kit's own pixel-trail it has no still frame: the canvas is blank until a pointer moves.
entries.description: Pixelated cursor trail emitting fading squares with retro digital feel.

entries.name: Pixel Transition
entries.lite_reason: A grid of opaque squares toggled with opacity and transform; no blur, no WebGL, no fixed layers.
entries.touch_reason: Described as a hover reveal. The vendored source adds a tap toggle, but under the doctrine tap must be the reveal and hover only a preview; an original build makes tap primary.
entries.when: A pixel-grid dissolve swaps one face of a card for another on tap: a photo to its caption, a price to its detail. One per screen; both faces ship in the bundle.
entries.notes: Weight is for the gsap original; an original build is a CSS grid of squares with per-cell animation-delay from a CSS variable, toggled by a tap, about 1 KiB and no gsap. Both faces must be in the bundle. Hover may preview the dissolve but never be the only way to reveal.
entries.description: Pixel dissolve transition for content reveal on hover.

entries.name: Ribbons
entries.lite_reason: OGL WebGL renderer drawing a full-screen ribbon layer; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: A cursor trail: the ribbons exist only while a pointer moves. The source binds touchmove, but the finger covers the trail and the layer is empty at rest.
entries.when: Physics ribbons stream behind the pointer; there is no pointer in Messages and the layer is empty at rest, so the Kit does not use it.
entries.notes: Breaks touch-first (cursor-following effect with nothing to show when the finger lifts) and WebGL under lite. Not a background: it has no rest state, so there is no static frame for reduced motion either.
entries.description: Flowing responsive ribbons/cursor trail driven by physics and pointer motion.

entries.name: Ripple Distortion
entries.lite_reason: OGL displacement shader over an image texture; WebGL is forbidden under lite and the wake animates continuously.
entries.touch_reason: Pointer-move drives the wake. The source also ripples on pointer-down, but the described effect is a following distortion, not a tap response.
entries.when: A water-displacement shader warps an image under the pointer and trails a wake; a pointer-following distortion on a WebGL canvas has no place in a touch-only, lite-first card.
entries.notes: Breaks touch-first (pointer-following) and WebGL under lite. The undistorted image is a valid still frame, which is why reduced_motion stays static. If a recipe ever wants a single tap-ripple on a hero photo, revisit as a pack candidate with a static poster fallback; the described effect is not that.
entries.description: Pointer-driven water displacement that warps content and leaves a decaying wake.

entries.name: Scroll Expand
entries.lite_reason: CSS clip-path and transform on one media frame; nothing in it is non-lite, the trigger is the problem.
entries.touch_reason: Scrolling works with a finger; the effect is driven by scroll position, not by a pointer.
entries.when: A rounded media frame grows to full bleed as the page scrolls; nothing moves on scroll inside the webview, so the Kit does not use it. Use a full-bleed .hero from the start.
entries.notes: Breaks 'nothing moves on scroll' (a scroll-linked reveal). The Messages webview also reports scroll position unreliably during its own rubber-banding, so the frame would jump.
entries.description: A rounded media frame that grows to full bleed as it scrolls through the viewport.

entries.name: Shape Blur
entries.lite_reason: Three.js WebGLRenderer running a blur shader; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The effect occurs on hover and follows pointer-move; the description gives no tap equivalent and the shape is invisible at rest.
entries.when: A blurred geometric outline morphs toward the pointer on hover; hover-only and Three-rendered, it fails touch-first and lite. For an ambient blob use fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg.
entries.notes: Breaks touch-first (hover-only reveal) and WebGL under lite. Invisible at rest, so no static frame exists. The ambient reading of it, a soft morphing blob behind a panel, is already fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg.
entries.description: Morphing blurred geometric shape. The effect occurs on hover.

entries.name: Splash Cursor
entries.lite_reason: Self-contained WebGL fluid simulation filling the viewport; WebGL is forbidden under lite and it is the heaviest GPU load in the set.
entries.touch_reason: Splashes follow the cursor. The source listens to touch as well, but the effect is a full-page pointer-following fluid layer with nothing at rest.
entries.when: A fluid-simulation splash bursts under the cursor and curls into waves; a full-page cursor effect on WebGL is off-limits in Messages.
entries.notes: Breaks touch-first (cursor-following), WebGL under lite, and the full-page physics playground rule. Blank until a pointer moves, so no static frame. No dependencies, roughly 25 KiB of shader and sim code, but size is not the issue.
entries.description: Liquid splash burst at cursor with curling ripples and waves.

entries.name: Star Border
entries.lite_reason: Pure CSS: two radial-gradient blobs orbit inside an overflow-hidden pill; no blur, no WebGL, no fixed layers.
entries.touch_reason: An ambient loop that needs no pointer; the button underneath is an ordinary tap target.
entries.when: A sparkle border orbits a button to mark the one action that matters; libraries/border-beam already does this around a card or CTA, so use it and keep it to one per screen.
entries.notes: Same mechanism as border-beam: a gradient travelling around a rounded edge. A button-sized variant is a size and radius prop on border-beam, not a new component. The loop is aria-hidden decoration and must pause under reduced motion.
entries.description: Animated star / sparkle border orbiting content with twinkle pulses.

entries.name: Sticker Peel
entries.lite_reason: CSS 3D transform, clip-path and a shadow on one image; no blur layer, no WebGL. The drop-shadow filter falls back to a box shadow under pixel/lite.
entries.touch_reason: The peel is an interaction rather than a hover; the source binds touchstart and Draggable drag, so tap-to-peel and finger drag both work.
entries.when: A sticker whose corner lifts and peels when you tap or drag it: a 'going' badge on an RSVP, a 'confirmed' seal on a receipt. One per screen; the image lives in the bundle.
entries.notes: Weight is for the gsap+Draggable original; an original build is a CSS 3D rotate on the corner, clip-path for the peeled flap and a transform-driven shadow, with pointer events for drag, about 2 KiB and no gsap. Needs a bundled PNG or SVG sticker the owner supplies from public/; never a remote image.
entries.description: Sticker corner lift + peel interaction using 3D transform and shadow depth.

entries.name: Strands
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader background filling its canvas and animating continuously; WebGL is forbidden under lite and backgrounds are non-lite by default.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient; the description names no pointer input and the source binds none.
entries.when: Glowing strands ripple and weave behind a landing hero; build it as a few translucent Canvas 2D curves so it stays lite, and reach for packed Beams or Silk only when a recipe wants the shader look.
entries.notes: Original build: four to six sine-offset bezier curves on a Canvas 2D at DPR 1, stroked two or three times at widening lineWidth and falling alpha with globalCompositeOperation lighter for the glow, no shadowBlur, about 1.5 KiB, and it renders one frame and stops under reduced motion. Packing is not justified: the look does not need a shader, and the shader mood is already covered by packed Beams, Silk and Light Rays. Renderer, lite and weight above describe the React Bits source, not the rebuild.
entries.description: Glowing ribbon-like strands that ripple and weave across a transparent canvas.

entries.name: Swarm Cursor
entries.lite_reason: OGL particle renderer covering the viewport and animating continuously; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The flock chases the pointer and scatters into an empty field at rest. The source has pointer-down, but the effect is defined by cursor-chasing.
entries.when: A flocking particle swarm chases the pointer and scatters at rest; a cursor-following WebGL layer has no role on a touch-only card in Messages.
entries.notes: Breaks touch-first (cursor-following) and WebGL under lite. A scattered field with no pointer says nothing, so there is no static frame. A tap-scatter flock could be a Canvas 2D mechanic inside a game-2d recipe, but that is a game, not this component.
entries.description: Flocking particle swarm that chases the pointer, jostles for space and drifts apart at rest.

entries.name: Target Cursor
entries.lite_reason: Four DOM corners on a fixed overlay moved with transforms; nothing non-lite in it, it is simply pointless without a cursor.
entries.touch_reason: Replaces the mouse cursor and snaps to hovered targets; there is no cursor on iOS and the source's touchstart only hides it.
entries.when: Four corner brackets replace the mouse cursor and snap onto hovered targets; Messages has no cursor, so the Kit does not use it. Use a focus ring on the .item instead.
entries.notes: Breaks touch-first: a custom cursor is a hover-only affordance with nothing to show on touch, and with no pointer position there is nothing to draw, so no static frame. The bracket-snap idea survives as a static selected-state ring on a .item or .tile.
entries.description: A cursor follow animation with 4 corners that lock onto targets.

entries.name: Acid Squares
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen shader tunnel; WebGL is forbidden under lite and a receding corridor needs a still plate there.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient zoom needs no pointer; nothing is hidden behind hover.
entries.when: A square tunnel receding into depth behind a title; build it as concentric squares scaling in Canvas 2D for a game title screen, not as a page-wide shader.
entries.notes: The React Bits version is a refractive 'crystalline' shader; the idea (nested squares zooming toward the viewer) is about 1 KiB of Canvas 2D or CSS perspective transforms. Drop the refraction, cap DPR at 1, hold one frame of nested squares under reduced motion. Restricted Prism/Beams already give a 'depth' hero, so build only when a game title screen wants it.
entries.description: A crystalline corridor of stacked squares receding into depth.

entries.name: Aero Shards
entries.lite_reason: GPU-driven instanced 3D shards; WebGL and DPR>1 are forbidden under lite, so it needs a flat plate fallback.
entries.touch_reason: Wind-driven idle motion carries the effect; the pointer interaction only enhances and is dropped or bound to touch-move.
entries.when: A 3D field of folded foil shards drifting behind a landing or product hero; non-lite, one per app, flat plate under lite and reduced motion.
entries.notes: Worth packing: lit, folded 3D geometry moved by wind cannot be rebuilt honestly in CSS or Canvas 2D, and 'content-safe placements' means it is designed to sit behind copy. Distinct from the packed metallics (Liquid Chrome, Molten Metal) because it is discrete shards, not a fluid surface. Pack with pointer input off by default and a static poster frame.
entries.description: A GPU-driven wind sculpture of folded foil shards with crisp detail, content-safe placements, and responsive pointer interactions.

entries.name: Aurora
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader background; the Kit's SVG gradient equivalent already renders flat under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient flow with no pointer dependency.
entries.when: Slow ribbons of color flowing behind a headline; use fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg in aurora tones instead of a shader.
entries.notes: Aurora is a flowing gradient; the Kit's SVG gradient blobs with teal/violet stops on the dark canvas read the same at 390px. If a shader-grade version is ever wanted, Grainient and Silk in the restricted set already cover flowing gradients, so no new pack.
entries.description: Flowing aurora gradient background.

entries.name: Balatro
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen paint-swirl shader; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The swirl is ambient; 'interactive' is a pointer enhancement it does not depend on.
entries.when: The swirling paint shader from the game Balatro; it reproduces another product's identity, so it stays out of every mini-app.
entries.notes: Rule broken: trade dress (exclusions section 4 — recreations of other products' identities are not harvested; same class as arlan's amo, midjourney, figma). It is also a heavy full-screen shader. For a swirl look use Liquid Chrome, Silk or Iridescence from the restricted set.
entries.description: The balatro shader, fully customizalbe and interactive.

entries.name: Ballpit
entries.lite_reason: Three.js scene with a real-time physics loop and lighting; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: As described the simulation runs on its own; the upstream cursor-follow sphere has no touch equivalent and would be disabled.
entries.when: A 3D physics ball pit filling the page; too heavy and too playful for a 390px card in Messages, so it stays out.
entries.notes: Rule broken: giant full-page physics playground (three plus a physics loop, far over the heavy line) behind a single-column card; every sphere moves forever, which also fights the one-hero-motion rule. If a game-3d template wants bouncing spheres, that is game code the Builder writes, not a background.
entries.description: Physics ball pit simulation with bouncing colorful spheres.

entries.name: Beams
entries.lite_reason: Three.js scene; the restricted build falls back to a flat plate under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient ribbons with no pointer dependency.
entries.when: Crossing light ribbons behind a landing or product hero; compiled from the restricted artifact, non-lite, one per app.
entries.notes: Already in the restricted artifact. Nothing to do beyond confirming the static poster frame and the lite plate in the catalog entry.
entries.description: Crossing animated ribbons with customizable properties.

entries.name: Color Bends
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader background; the Kit's SVG gradient equivalent renders flat under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient flow; any upstream mouse influence is optional and off.
entries.when: Bands of vivid color bending and flowing behind a panel; use fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg, or Grainient from the restricted set for the richer look.
entries.notes: A flowing multi-stop gradient. The Kit's SVG gradient blobs cover it at card size; Grainient, Iridescence and Silk already cover the shader-grade version, so no new pack.
entries.description: Vibrant color bends with smooth flowing animation.

entries.name: CRT Warp
entries.lite_reason: Full-canvas plasma with barrel distortion and bloom; shader only, forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The plasma runs ambient; the pointer interaction is an enhancement to disable.
entries.when: A curved CRT plasma with scanlines and bloom for a retro game title screen; non-lite, one per app, flat frame under reduced motion, pointer part off.
entries.notes: Low-priority candidate: plasma plus barrel warp plus bloom genuinely needs a shader, and a retro game-2d title screen is a legitimate use. But Faulty Terminal (packed) already owns the CRT look; take this only if the game-2d template wants a plasma screen rather than terminal squares. Disable pointer input in the pack.
entries.description: Full-canvas CRT plasma with curved distortion, scanlines, bloom and pointer interaction.

entries.name: Dark Veil
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader with postprocessing (noise, scanlines, warp); under lite the flat atmosphere canvas is the veil.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient drift with no pointer dependency.
entries.when: A barely moving dark haze behind a chat or tool screen; the atmosphere canvas with fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg in dark tones already gives it.
entries.notes: In a mini-app the warm dark atmosphere canvas is already the veil; add the Kit's SVG gradient with two near-canvas stops for drift. Under lite and the pixel theme it is just the flat canvas, which is correct.
entries.description: Subtle dark background with a smooth animation and postprocessing.

entries.name: Dither
entries.lite_reason: Three/R3F shader with a postprocessing pass; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient noise; the upstream mouse-wave option stays off.
entries.when: Retro dithered noise drifting behind a pixel-styled hero or 2D game; compiled from the restricted artifact, non-lite, one per app.
entries.notes: Already in the restricted artifact. Keep the mouse-wave option off by default; a Bayer dither over a still gradient is the reduced-motion frame.
entries.description: Retro dithered noise shader background.

entries.name: Dot Field
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen animated canvas with glow and sparkle; a still dot grid is the lite fallback.
entries.touch_reason: Bulge, glow and sparkle follow the cursor; a finger covers the very spot that reacts, and there is no cursor on touch.
entries.when: A dot grid that bulges and sparkles under the cursor; on touch use fancy/pixel-trail, and a plain dot grid is one CSS radial-gradient.
entries.notes: Cursor-driven; the Kit's pixel-trail is the finger-safe version of the same idea. The ambient 'wave' variant is trivial in Canvas 2D but is a full-screen loop, so it must be aria-hidden decoration and freeze under reduced motion.
entries.description: Interactive dot grid with cursor bulge, glow, sparkle, and wave effects.

entries.name: Dot Grid
entries.lite_reason: Animated full-screen canvas driven by a GSAP inertia loop; a still dot grid is the lite fallback.
entries.touch_reason: Dots react to cursor position and velocity; no tap or drag equivalent is described.
entries.when: A dot grid that shoves away from the cursor; on touch use fancy/pixel-trail, and a still dot grid is one CSS radial-gradient.
entries.notes: Needs GSAP (heavy) for a cursor effect touch cannot use. A tap ripple is the only touch-native part and is a 20-line build-original if wanted; the static grid is background-image: radial-gradient.
entries.description: Animated dot grid with cursor interactions.

entries.name: Evil Eye
entries.lite_reason: Procedural shader with a bloom-style glow; the SVG rebuild is lite once the blur filter is dropped.
entries.touch_reason: Iris and pupil animate on their own; no pointer dependency described.
entries.when: A single animated eye with a slit pupil and fiery glow as a hero mark; draw it in SVG with a dilating pupil and one glow, one per screen.
entries.notes: A fixed-size mark, not a background, so it does not need a shader: radial-gradient iris, an ellipse pupil animated on transform (scaleX) for the slit, a feGaussianBlur glow in orange. Cultural motif, not trade dress. Turn the glow filter off under lite and hold the open-eye frame under reduced motion.
entries.description: Procedural evil eye shader with animated iris, slit pupil, and fiery outer glow.

entries.name: Faulty Terminal
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader; WebGL is forbidden under lite, so the restricted build shows a flat plate.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient flicker; the upstream mouseReact option stays off.
entries.when: Flickering CRT terminal squares behind a status or retro game screen; compiled from the restricted artifact, non-lite, one per app.
entries.notes: Already in the restricted artifact. Keep mouseReact off; flicker must stop entirely under reduced motion, leaving the scanline grid as the still frame.
entries.description: Terminal CRT scanline squares effect with flicker + noise.

entries.name: Ferrofluid
entries.lite_reason: Fluid-field shader with glowing contour lines; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The fluid churns on its own; the cursor magnet is an enhancement that ships off or bound to touch-drag, so nothing is lost on a phone.
entries.when: Churning fluid drawn as glowing contour lines behind a landing hero; non-lite, one per app, cursor magnet off or bound to a drag.
entries.notes: Low-priority candidate: a fluid field with marching contour lines needs a shader, and the topographic look is distinct from Liquid Ether, Liquid Chrome and Molten Metal. Pack only with the magnet disabled by default (bind to touch-drag if kept) and a static contour frame for lite and reduced motion. If the pack list is tight, skip it: Liquid Ether already gives a fluid hero.
entries.description: A churning magnetic fluid traced by glowing contour lines, with a cursor magnet.

entries.name: Floating Lines
entries.lite_reason: Three.js WebGL scene used as a full-screen animated background; lite forbids WebGL and DPR>1.
entries.touch_reason: The lines bend and drift toward the cursor; no tap or drag equivalent is described, so on touch only the idle drift remains.
entries.when: Three.js lines that drift and bend toward the cursor; skip it in a mini-app, since Messages has no cursor and the packed Beams background already gives ambient light lines.
entries.notes: Rules broken: cursor-following (touch first; hover may enhance, never reveal) and WebGL under lite. The idle drift alone does not justify a Three scene on a 390px card; for ambient light lines use @kit/restricted/beams, which is already packed.
entries.description: 3D floating lines that react to cursor movement.

entries.name: Galaxy
entries.lite_reason: OGL fragment-shader starfield covering the whole surface; under lite render a plain var(--canvas) plate.
entries.touch_reason: The starfield twinkles and rotates on its own; pointer parallax and repulsion are enhancements to switch off on touch.
entries.when: Twinkling starfield behind a launch countdown or night-event hero; one per app, aria-hidden, never under lite, with pointer parallax switched off.
entries.notes: Already in the restricted artifact as @kit/restricted/galaxy. Its 'parallax' is pointer parallax, not scroll, so it does not break the nothing-moves-on-scroll rule. Freeze to one frame under reduced motion.
entries.description: Parallax realistic starfield with pointer interactions.

entries.name: Ghost Fibers
entries.lite_reason: Recursive fiber field is a fragment shader; full-screen animated background, so non-lite by Kit policy.
entries.touch_reason: No pointer input is described; the field twists and glows on its own.
entries.when: Deep-blue twisting fiber field with glowing bands; a calm atmospheric backdrop for a landing hero or evening invite when the packed Silk and Beams feel too plain.
entries.notes: Genuinely needs a shader (recursive noise, radial twist, bloom), so not a build-original. Low-priority candidate: mood overlaps packed Silk and Beams; colors must map onto Air tokens. Must freeze to one frame under reduced motion and fall back to var(--canvas) under lite. Compiled-only via the restricted artifact, never in git. Renderer library (three vs ogl) is a guess.
entries.description: A deep-blue recursive fiber field with luminous bands, radial twisting and soft atmospheric glow.

entries.name: Gradient Blinds
entries.lite_reason: Source is an OGL shader with noise distortion over the full surface; a pure-CSS stripe original would be lite-capable.
entries.touch_reason: The spotlight follows the pointer; without a pointer the blinds are a static stripe field, so the described interaction has no touch meaning.
entries.when: Bold diagonal gradient stripes behind a store or landing hero when a flat token gradient feels too quiet; the pointer spotlight means nothing on touch, so leave it out.
entries.notes: Original approach: repeating-linear-gradient stripes over a two-stop token gradient, a fixed radial highlight in place of the cursor spotlight, optional SVG feTurbulence displacement for grain that is skipped under lite. The CSS original is light and lite-capable; the source's weight is the OGL runtime.
entries.description: Layered gradient blinds with spotlight and noise distortion.

entries.name: Gradient Waves
entries.lite_reason: Raymarched fragment shader over the full surface; non-lite. An SVG layered-wave original can render flat and still under lite.
entries.touch_reason: No pointer input described; the waves roll on their own.
entries.when: Stacked sine waves rolling toward a hazy horizon; a calm hero backdrop for a landing or countdown screen where the slow roll is the only motion, flat and still under lite.
entries.notes: The look (stacked waves fading to a horizon) does not need raymarching: three to five SVG sine paths with shrinking amplitude and spacing, a token gradient fill and one slow transform loop read as the same landscape at 390px. Only the shader lighting is lost. Revisit as a pack candidate only if that SVG build is judged not enough. Library guess uncertain.
entries.description: Raymarched sine waves rolling toward a soft, hazy horizon.

entries.name: Grainient
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader with grain and wave distortion over the full surface; lite falls back to a flat CSS gradient.
entries.touch_reason: Ambient swirl with no pointer dependency.
entries.when: Grainy swirling gradient with soft wave distortion; the packed painterly backdrop for a landing or store hero with one display line over it.
entries.notes: Already packed as @kit/restricted/grainient. Under lite or the pixel theme use fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg rendered flat, or a plain token gradient. Freeze one frame under reduced motion.
entries.description: Grainy gradient swirls with soft wave distortion.

entries.name: Grid Distortion
entries.lite_reason: Three.js mesh warping an image texture; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The warp exists only while the cursor moves over the mesh; no tap or drag equivalent is described.
entries.when: An image whose mesh warps under the cursor; skip it in a mini-app, since the distortion exists only while a pointer moves and Messages has no pointer.
entries.notes: Rules broken: cursor-following with no touch equivalent (hover may enhance, never reveal) and WebGL under lite. The effect needs an image texture, which the owner would supply from public/ (not a CSP risk, just a required asset). For a textured still image use fancy/pixelate-svg-filter or a CSS filter.
entries.description: Warped grid mesh distorts smoothly reacting to cursor.

entries.name: Grid Motion
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen animated tile background on an oversized rotated layer; non-lite by Kit policy and sized for desktop widths.
entries.touch_reason: Row offsets are driven by the pointer's horizontal position; nothing moves without a cursor.
entries.when: Rows of tiles that slide with the pointer's position; skip it in a mini-app, since there is no pointer on touch and a drifting wall of tiles fights the single column.
entries.notes: Rules broken: cursor-following, and a desktop-width composition (rotated, oversized grid) that does not fit a 390px single column. The description says 'grid lines' but the component is rows of tiles moved by GSAP, so renderer is dom. For a moving strip of images use fancy/simple-marquee; for a swipeable set use fancy/simple-carousel.
entries.description: Perspective moving grid lines based on cusror position.

entries.name: Grid Scan
entries.lite_reason: Source is a Three.js room with bloom; a CSS 3D original with gradient grid faces can render a still frame under lite.
entries.touch_reason: The scan sweep runs on its own; the 'cool interactions' are pointer tilt, an enhancement to disable on touch.
entries.when: A perspective grid room with one light plane sweeping through it; the hero backdrop for a retro game or tool screen, with the sweep as the screen's single hero motion.
entries.notes: Original approach: a preserve-3d container with floor and wall faces filled by repeating-linear-gradient grids in var(--accent), and a single translating scan bar with a gradient glow; no filter: blur under lite. The Three version adds only bloom. Keep the sweep finite or aria-hidden; under reduced motion show the room with the bar at rest. Source weight is the Three runtime; the CSS original is light.
entries.description: Animated grid room 3D scan effect and cool interactions.

entries.name: Hyperspeed
entries.lite_reason: Full-page Three.js scene with postprocessing bloom; far over the lite ceiling.
entries.touch_reason: Streaks move continuously without input; the speed-up is press-and-hold, which has a touch equivalent but collides with iOS long-press callouts inside Messages.
entries.when: Light streaks racing at the viewer, faster while held; skip it in a mini-app, since it is a heavy full-page Three scene with bloom and the hold gesture collides with iOS long-press.
entries.notes: Rules broken: heavy (three plus postprocessing, a giant full-page playground per the exclusions), an infinite loop as the whole screen rather than aria-hidden decoration, and a hold gesture that fights the webview's long-press behaviour. If a launch moment is wanted, use the packed Galaxy with a one-shot CSS scale on the hero.
entries.description: Animated lines continuously moving to simulate hyperspace travel on click hold.

entries.name: Iridescence
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader over the full surface; lite gets a flat canvas and arlan/color-depth's glossy material on the button instead.
entries.touch_reason: The waves shift on their own; the optional pointer reaction stays off on touch.
entries.when: Pearlescent shader with slow shifting waves; the packed glossy backdrop for a product or store hero that wants a material feel behind a single display line.
entries.notes: Already packed as @kit/restricted/iridescence. Map its color to var(--accent). Under reduced motion freeze one frame; under lite render nothing behind the panel.
entries.description: Slick iridescent shader with shifting waves.

entries.name: Letter Glitch
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen continuously animating canvas background; non-lite by Kit policy. The original should draw one static frame of glyphs at DPR 1 under lite.
entries.touch_reason: No pointer dependency; glyphs swap on a timer.
entries.when: Matrix-style grid of glyphs flickering on a 2D canvas; build an original for a terminal-themed game or tool backdrop, in the system mono font, finite and aria-hidden.
entries.notes: Simple to rebuild: a canvas 2D grid of glyphs in var(--font-ui) or system monospace (no web font), random cell swaps at a fixed interval, and a CSS radial-gradient overlay for the vignette instead of a shader. Loop must be finite or aria-hidden. The packed Faulty Terminal covers the CRT look if a shader is wanted.
entries.description: Matrix style letter animation.

entries.name: Light Pillar
entries.lite_reason: Source is a Three.js shader with bloom; a CSS gradient-column original renders flat, without blur, under lite.
entries.touch_reason: No pointer input described; the pillar glows and pulses on its own.
entries.when: One glowing vertical column of light behind a headline or countdown number; use it when a hero needs a focal glow without a shader, flat and unblurred under lite.
entries.notes: Original approach: a narrow linear-gradient column from transparent through var(--accent) and back, with two wider low-opacity copies for the glow; an optional slow opacity breathe is the one hero motion; no filter: blur under lite. The packed Light Rays covers the volumetric variant. Source weight is the Three runtime; the CSS original is light.
entries.description: Vertical pillar of light with glow effects.

entries.name: Light Rays
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader over the full surface; lite uses a flat CSS linear or conic gradient fan from the top edge.
entries.touch_reason: Rays animate on their own; the optional pointer-follow stays off.
entries.when: Volumetric rays falling from a chosen edge; the packed backdrop for a confirmation or reveal hero where light from above is the only motion on the screen.
entries.notes: Already packed as @kit/restricted/light-rays. Keep followMouse off, set the origin to the top edge for the compact card, and freeze one frame under reduced motion.
entries.description: Volumetric light rays/beams with customizable direction.

entries.name: Light Tunnel
entries.lite_reason: Source is a full-screen shader tunnel; a canvas 2D original of radial strands can show one still frame at DPR 1 under lite.
entries.touch_reason: No pointer input described; pulses race on their own.
entries.when: Radial strands converging to a vanishing point with pulses racing inward; a loud launch or game hero backdrop, one pulse cycle as the hero motion, still under reduced motion.
entries.notes: The fibre-optic read is many thin bright lines from a center point with brighter segments moving along them; canvas 2D draws that directly, with a radial gradient for depth fog, so no shader is needed. Keep it aria-hidden decoration with a finite pulse loop; a tunnel is loud, so it is the screen's one hero motion. Source weight is the Three runtime; the canvas original is light.
entries.description: A radial fibre-optic tunnel with light pulses racing into depth.

entries.name: Lightfall
entries.lite_reason: OGL fragment-shader tunnel rendered at device DPR; WebGL is forbidden on lite and there is no CSS fallback.
entries.touch_reason: The streak rain runs without a pointer, but the cursor light half of the effect needs a held finger over the background, which is not a Messages gesture.
entries.when: A tunnel of colored light streaks raining toward the viewer; use once as the splash hero of a game-3d or launch screen when Beams and Light Rays feel too calm.
entries.notes: Overlaps packed Beams, Light Rays and Side Rays, so pack only if a template asks for a hyperspace look. Drop the cursor light on touch. The component does not check prefers-reduced-motion; the restricted wrapper must freeze one frame and force DPR 1.
entries.description: Colorful light streaks raining down a glowing tunnel with a cursor light.

entries.name: Lightning
entries.lite_reason: Raw WebGL fragment shader (no library); WebGL is forbidden on lite. An original Canvas 2D bolt would be lite.
entries.touch_reason: Time-driven; no pointer input.
entries.when: A branching lightning bolt with glow flicker; strike once as the hero moment of a storm, power-up or countdown-hits-zero screen, never as a permanent flashing loop.
entries.notes: Rebuild on Canvas 2D: midpoint-displacement polyline with two or three branches, shadowBlur glow, one-shot flicker under 300ms. Keep flashes under three per second and, under reduced motion, draw the bolt once and stop. No library needed.
entries.description: Procedural lightning bolts with branching and glow flicker.

entries.name: Line Waves
entries.lite_reason: OGL full-screen shader; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Waves animate on their own; the mouse warp is an enhancement lost on touch, not a reveal.
entries.when: Stacked sine lines that ripple across a panel with a slow color shift; use as a calm ambient header behind a title when a gradient blob feels too soft.
entries.notes: Rebuild as 8-12 SVG polylines or Canvas 2D paths displaced by a sine function; pure lite, under 2 KiB. Only the shader's warped-color distortion is lost.
entries.description: Animated line wave pattern with colorful warped distortion.

entries.name: Liquid Chrome
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader surface; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Flows on its own and handles touchmove exactly as it handles mousemove.
entries.when: A flowing chrome surface behind a hero word or product; import @kit/restricted/liquid-chrome for one non-lite hero, or reach for libraries/metal-fx when you need Tier A.
entries.notes: Already in the restricted artifact. Tier A near-equivalent is libraries/metal-fx (liquid-metal plate with a flat fallback). No reduced-motion check inside; the wrapper freezes one frame.
entries.description: Liquid metallic chrome shader with flowing reflective surface.

entries.name: Liquid Ether
entries.lite_reason: Three.js fluid simulation with render targets; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Handles touchstart/touchmove alongside mouse events and idles with its own flow when nobody touches.
entries.when: Fluid color that swirls under a finger and drifts on its own; import @kit/restricted/liquid-ether for a non-lite landing hero that invites a touch.
entries.notes: Already packed. Heaviest of this chunk (three plus a fluid sim, ~38 KiB source); pauses offscreen via IntersectionObserver. Force DPR 1 on phones and allow one instance per app.
entries.description: Interactive liquid shader with flowing distortion and customizable colors.

entries.name: Molten Metal
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader plasma; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Swirls on its own; the mouse influence is an enhancement lost on touch.
entries.when: Molten plasma filaments with white-hot cores; import @kit/restricted/molten-metal for a dramatic non-lite game or launch hero, one per app.
entries.notes: Already packed. Pauses offscreen via IntersectionObserver; no reduced-motion check inside, so the wrapper freezes a frame.
entries.description: Swirling caustic plasma filaments with molten, white-hot cores.

entries.name: Orb
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader orb at device DPR; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: The orb floats on its own, but the hover distortion the description sells has no touch equivalent (mousemove only).
entries.when: A glowing energy orb that warps under the pointer; the Kit already has aicss/orbs for an ambient presence and libraries/thinking-orbs for named states, so use those.
entries.notes: aicss/orbs is a lite CSS orb; libraries/thinking-orbs adds nine named agent states on Canvas 2D. Neither needs WebGL, so there is no reason to pack this one.
entries.description: Floating energy orb with customizable hover effect.

entries.name: Particles
entries.lite_reason: OGL 3D point cloud; WebGL is forbidden on lite. An original Canvas 2D field would be lite.
entries.touch_reason: Particles drift on their own; the mouse parallax is a lost enhancement.
entries.when: A field of drifting dots behind a hero or empty state; draw a few dozen on Canvas 2D at DPR 1, aria-hidden, and stop them under reduced motion.
entries.notes: The same read comes from 40-80 Canvas 2D circles with slow velocity and soft alpha; no library. fancy/pixel-trail already covers the pointer-reactive variant.
entries.description: Configurable particle system.

entries.name: Pixel Blast
entries.lite_reason: Three.js scene with an EffectComposer liquid pass; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: pointerdown and click spawn a burst, so a tap works like a click.
entries.when: Chunky pixel bursts that ripple out from a tap; rebuild on Canvas 2D as tap feedback in a game or a one-shot celebration when a form confirms.
entries.notes: Three plus postprocessing exist only for the optional liquid pass. The burst itself is a grid of squares expanding from the tap point with a short lifetime, trivial on Canvas 2D. Skip the liquid post-process.
entries.description: Exploding pixel particle bursts with optional liquid postprocessing.

entries.name: Pixel Snow
