entries.lite_reason: Three.js shader quad; WebGL is forbidden on lite. An original Canvas 2D version would be lite.
entries.touch_reason: Time-driven; no pointer input.
entries.when: Pixelated snow drifting down behind a card; rebuild on Canvas 2D for a seasonal invite or countdown, aria-hidden, frozen to a still scatter under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Three is overkill for falling squares; 60-120 rects with a slow y velocity and a sideways wobble on Canvas 2D reads the same and is lite. The original pauses offscreen via IntersectionObserver; do the same.
entries.description: Falling pixelated snow effect with customizable density and speed.

entries.name: Plasma
entries.lite_reason: OGL full-screen shader; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Swirls on its own; the mouse influence is optional.
entries.when: Soft plasma gradients that swirl and morph; fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg gives the same ambient wash in lite CSS, and packed Grainient or Silk give the shader look.
entries.notes: One of the few React Bits backgrounds that honors prefers-reduced-motion itself. Redundant three ways: Tier A gradient blobs, packed Grainient, packed Silk.
entries.description: Organic plasma gradients swirl + morph with smooth turbulence.

entries.name: Plasma Wave
entries.lite_reason: OGL raymarched mesh at device DPR; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Time-driven; no pointer input.
entries.when: Raymarched plasma sheets with two interfering waves; a non-lite hero for a game-3d or launch screen when Molten Metal and Silk are already spoken for.
entries.notes: Needs a shader, so it cannot be rebuilt, but it sits close to packed Molten Metal, Silk and Liquid Ether. Low-priority candidate; raymarching is costly on phone GPUs, so force DPR 1. No reduced-motion check inside.
entries.description: Raymarched plasma waves with dual-wave interference and OGL.

entries.name: Prism
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader prism; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Rotates on its own in the default mode; the pointer-follow mode is optional.
entries.when: A rotating glass prism throwing colored light; import @kit/restricted/prism as the one non-lite hero of a landing or store screen.
entries.notes: Already packed. Pauses offscreen via IntersectionObserver; use its rotate mode, not hover, on phones.
entries.description: Rotating prism with configurable intensity, size, and colors.

entries.name: Prismatic Burst
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader with a generated gradient texture; WebGL is forbidden on lite.
entries.touch_reason: Rotates on its own by default; the pointer-follow mode is optional.
entries.when: Rainbow rays bursting from a center point; rebuild as a slowly rotating CSS conic-gradient sunburst under a radial mask for a celebration or reveal hero.
entries.notes: The shader adds distortion and a texture lookup that a CSS sunburst loses; when a shader look is wanted, packed Light Rays and Side Rays already exist. A conic-gradient with transform: rotate is lite and stops cleanly under reduced motion.
entries.description: Burst of light rays with controllable color, distortion, amount.

entries.name: Radar
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader as shipped; WebGL is forbidden on lite. The SVG rebuild is lite.
entries.touch_reason: Sweeps on its own; the mouse offset is a lost enhancement.
entries.when: Concentric rings, spokes and a sweeping beam; rebuild in SVG with a rotating conic-gradient wedge as the searching state of a status or chat screen.
entries.notes: Pure geometry: circles, lines and one conic-gradient wedge rotating with transform; under 1 KiB and lite. Competes with the libraries/thinking-orbs searching state, so pick one per screen. OGL is unnecessary for this.
entries.description: Radar sweep effect with concentric rings, radial spokes, and a rotating beam.

entries.name: Ripple Grid
entries.lite_reason: OGL fragment-shader background running full-bleed; WebGL is forbidden under lite and animated backgrounds are non-lite by default.
entries.touch_reason: The ripple loop runs on its own; the optional pointer-follow is a hover enhancement that a mini-app drops or maps to touchmove, never a requirement.
entries.when: A grid whose lines ripple outward in slow rings; an ambient backdrop for one hero screen of a tool or game lobby, never behind body copy.
entries.notes: Concept is a grid of lines displaced by a radial sine; Canvas 2D or an SVG with stroke offsets rebuilds it in under 3 KiB with no shader. Original build: draw one still frame under reduced motion and lite, animate only the displacement phase otherwise, aria-hidden. Do not port the vendored OGL version; the packed set already carries enough GPU plates.
entries.description: A grid that continuously animates with a ripple effect.

entries.name: Scanner
entries.lite_reason: Shader-driven interference bands rendered full-screen; treated as a WebGL animated background and therefore non-lite.
entries.touch_reason: Bands sweep autonomously; nothing depends on a pointer.
entries.when: Soft interference bands sweep the panel like an oscilloscope trace; use as the ambient plate behind a working or scanning status, one per screen.
entries.notes: Two or three repeating-linear-gradient layers moved with transform and a slow opacity pulse give the same calm scan-line read in pure CSS, which would even qualify as lite. Cap it to the compact card height, pause the loop under reduced motion (a single frame of bands is complete), and never place it behind body copy. Renderer inferred from the description's shader-style wording; confidence medium on the vendored implementation, high on the judgment.
entries.description: Calm interference bands sweeping across the screen like an oscilloscope.

entries.name: Shape Grid
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen continuously animated background; non-lite by the Kit's default for animated plates even though it likely avoids WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Shapes drift in a configured direction on their own; any hover tint is an enhancement, not a reveal.
entries.when: A field of small squares, hexagons, circles or triangles drifting in one direction; a quiet decorative plate behind a hero card or lobby.
entries.notes: A tiled SVG pattern (one shape symbol, repeated) with a single translate keyframe is the whole effect; Canvas 2D if per-shape variation is wanted. Under reduced motion the pattern simply stops, which is a complete frame. Renderer is a medium-confidence inference; if the vendored version turns out to be a shader the disposition is unchanged, build it original.
entries.description: Animated grid with shape variants (square, hexagon, circle, triangle) + direction customization.

entries.name: Shape Waves
entries.lite_reason: Described as WebGPU; WebGPU sits above the WebGL ceiling and is not guaranteed in the Messages webview, so the vendored version is non-lite and needs a flat-plate fallback everywhere.
entries.touch_reason: Waves roll on their own; no pointer dependency in the description.
entries.when: Rows of tiny shapes brighten and swell as waves roll across them, optionally parting around a word; a hero plate for a landing or launch card.
entries.notes: WebGPU is not in the contract and cannot be packed as-is; do not add to the restricted allowlist. The concept, a grid of shapes whose scale and brightness follow sin(x+t), is a Canvas 2D loop; the text cutout is a destination-out fill of a system-font word, which keeps it free of web fonts. Draw one still frame under reduced motion and lite.
entries.description: A WebGPU field of triangles, circles and squares that brighten and grow along rolling waves, with an optional text cutout the waves flow around.

entries.name: Side Rays
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader background; the restricted wrapper renders a flat plate under lite, reduced motion or no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Rays animate autonomously with color and speed props; no pointer needed.
entries.when: Light rays fanning in from one edge behind a hero word or product shot; already packed as @kit/restricted/side-rays, non-lite, flat plate when off.
entries.notes: Already one of the 13 compiled-only React Bits backgrounds. Import from the restricted artifact only; it never lives in git. Sibling of Light Rays, pick one per app. One hero motion per screen means nothing else animates on the same screen.
entries.description: Animated light rays emanating from the side with customizable colors and speed.

entries.name: Silk
entries.lite_reason: React Three Fiber shader plane; WebGL is forbidden under lite, the restricted wrapper falls back to a flat gradient.
entries.touch_reason: Continuous wave loop with no pointer input.
entries.when: Slow silk-like waves with soft lighting behind a hero; already packed as @kit/restricted/silk, non-lite, renders a flat gradient when WebGL is off.
entries.notes: Already one of the 13 compiled-only React Bits backgrounds. Heaviest of the packed set because it drags in three and r3f; budget for it and use only one three-based plate per app. Under the pixel theme the flat fallback should read as var(--canvas), not a hard-coded color.
entries.description: Smooth waves background with soft lighting.

entries.name: Sliced Waves
entries.lite_reason: Glowing bars rendered by a shader full-screen; non-lite as a WebGL animated background.
entries.touch_reason: Bars ripple on a timer; no pointer dependency.
entries.when: A row of soft glowing bars that ripple like an equalizer; an ambient plate for a music, playlist or listening-party card, one per screen.
entries.notes: A dozen div bars with transform: scaleY driven by staggered keyframes and a box-shadow glow is the entire effect in CSS, and that version is lite-safe on the pixel theme with the glow off. Never fake real audio levels with it; it is decoration, aria-hidden, static under reduced motion. Renderer inferred from the glow wording; medium confidence.
entries.description: A grid of soft glowing bars rippling like a slatted equalizer.

entries.name: Soft Aurora
entries.lite_reason: Explicitly a shader with 3D Perlin noise; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Noise-driven drift with no pointer input.
entries.when: Slow aurora-like color drift behind a panel; reach for fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg, or a packed shader gradient (Grainient, Silk) when non-lite.
entries.notes: At 390px a blurred set of moving color blobs reads the same as a Perlin aurora, and the Tier A component already flattens under lite and the pixel theme. Grainient and Iridescence in the restricted set cover the true shader-gradient look, so a third soft-gradient shader adds no capability; do not add to the allowlist.
entries.description: Soft aurora borealis shader with 3D Perlin noise and cosine gradient palettes.

entries.name: Threads
entries.lite_reason: OGL shader drawing the line field full-screen; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Lines sway on their own; the optional pointer bend is an enhancement that is dropped on touch.
entries.when: Fine wavy lines that sway like woven fabric; an ambient plate behind a hero headline, drawn once as a still under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Twenty to forty polylines with a sine offset per vertex in Canvas 2D reproduce the fabric read with no dependency. Build one original 'flowing lines' plate with variants and let it also stand in for Waves and Web Threads rather than shipping three near-identical canvases. Keep line count low on the phone GPU and stop the loop under reduced motion.
entries.description: Animated pattern of lines forming a fabric-like motion.

entries.name: Topography
entries.lite_reason: Glowing contour lines from a noise field, shader-rendered full-screen; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Contours breathe on a timer; no pointer dependency.
entries.when: Glowing contour lines that slowly breathe like a living elevation map; a hero plate for a trip, hike, route or map-flavored card.
entries.notes: Build it original: a coarse value-noise grid (about 40x80 cells at 390px) run through marching squares on Canvas 2D, contour levels tinted by elevation with theme tokens, glow from two or three layered low-alpha strokes rather than shadowBlur. Advance the noise phase slowly and stop it under reduced motion, which leaves a complete still map; DPR 1 on lite. Distinct look from all 13 packed plates but not shader-dependent, so do not add to the restricted allowlist. Renderer inferred; medium confidence on the vendored implementation.
entries.description: A living contour map with glowing, elevation-tinted lines.

entries.name: Waves
entries.lite_reason: Full-screen per-frame Canvas 2D redraw of many noise-driven lines; non-lite by the Kit's default for animated backgrounds, though a still frame is lite-safe.
entries.touch_reason: Lines flow on their own; the pointer bulge is an optional enhancement that a touch build omits or maps to touchmove.
entries.when: Layered flowing lines with a gentle swell; a calm ambient plate behind a hero card, one per screen and still under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Same family as Threads and Web Threads; one original Canvas 2D 'flowing lines' plate with a density and swell prop covers all three. Keep the line count and DPR at 1 on lite, freeze the phase under reduced motion, and never let it run behind scrolling body copy. Renderer is a medium-confidence recollection of a 2D canvas implementation.
entries.description: Layered lines that form smooth wave patterns with animation.

entries.name: Web Threads
entries.lite_reason: Glowing sine threads with a luminous focal point, shader-rendered; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Threads oscillate autonomously around a fixed convergence point; no pointer needed.
entries.when: Glowing sine threads converging on a bright focal point; a hero plate for a launch or landing card that wants one luminous center.
entries.notes: A variant of the flowing-lines plate: sine polylines whose amplitude tapers toward a shared point, glow via layered low-alpha strokes rather than shadowBlur (cheap on the phone). Flat plate under lite and reduced motion. Renderer inferred from the glow wording; medium confidence.
entries.description: Glowing sine threads woven through a luminous convergence point.

entries.name: Accordion Gallery
entries.lite_reason: Flex-basis transitions and transformed images; no backdrop-filter, fixed background or WebGL implied.
entries.touch_reason: Panels widen on hover/focus and imagery parallaxes with pointer position; a tap can focus but captions would be hover-revealed and nothing parallaxes without a cursor.
entries.when: Hover-widening panels that reveal parallax imagery and captions; not for a mini-app, hover never reveals and there is no cursor to parallax, so a gallery uses fancy/simple-carousel.
entries.notes: Rules broken: hover-only reveal (hover may enhance, never reveal) and pointer parallax (touch first). A multi-panel horizontal accordion also collapses to ~40px slivers at 390px. Nearest Kit answer for the need is fancy/simple-carousel; images would have to be bundled regardless.
entries.description: Panels expand on hover or focus, revealing parallax imagery and captions.

entries.name: Animated List
entries.lite_reason: Opacity and transform stagger on DOM rows; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: Rows are tapped or scrolled like any list; the entrance needs no pointer.
entries.when: List rows that enter with a short stagger on mount; use it once as the hero motion when a guest list or task list first appears, never on scroll.
entries.notes: scroll_linked=true describes the source component: it reveals rows as they scroll into view inside their own container and fades the edges by scroll position, which the doctrine forbids (nothing moves on scroll). The description's trigger is entry, so the original is allowed and is trivial: CSS animation-delay on Air .row/.item, fired once on mount with no IntersectionObserver or scroll listener, finishing within ~300ms total. Under reduced motion every row is simply present.
entries.description: List items enter with staggered motion variants for polished reveals.

entries.name: Border Glow
entries.lite_reason: Conic/radial gradients and a mask on a pseudo-element driven by CSS variables; a filter blur is likely but not backdrop-filter.
entries.touch_reason: The glow follows cursor direction and intensifies near edges; without a pointer it has nothing to follow.
entries.when: A glowing border that chases the cursor; the Kit's border-beam already marks the one card that deserves attention without needing a pointer.
entries.notes: The need (highlight one card) is covered by libraries/border-beam, which animates on its own and is lite. The cursor-following part violates touch-first and is dropped; a static glow via box-shadow or var(--ring) is the lite fallback.
entries.description: Glowing mesh-gradient border that follows cursor direction and intensifies near edges.

entries.name: Bounce Cards
entries.lite_reason: Transform/opacity keyframes on a handful of image cards; no forbidden features.
entries.touch_reason: Entrance plays on mount; any hover-to-spread extra is an enhancement, not a reveal.
entries.when: A fan of cards that springs into place on mount; a hero motion for a gallery or product spread, settling to the same fanned layout under reduced motion.
entries.notes: React Bits pulls in GSAP for a spring; an original build is a CSS keyframe with an overshoot cubic-bezier and per-card delay, well under 1 KiB. Counts as the screen's one hero motion. Keep to 3-5 cards so the fan fits 390px; images are bundled.
entries.description: Cards bounce that bounce in on mount.

entries.name: Bubble Menu
entries.lite_reason: Scale/translate transitions on pill buttons; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: Opened and closed by tapping a toggle; items are ordinary buttons.
entries.when: A round toggle that expands into a staggered ring of action bubbles; use for a compact plus-menu of three to five actions, opened by tap.
entries.notes: React Bits uses GSAP for the stagger; an original is CSS transitions with transition-delay on each bubble and 44px targets. The React Bits version is a full-screen site nav overlay, which a single-screen mini-app does not need; scale it down to an action menu. libraries/liquid-gooey already does a droplet-style plus-menu if the goo look is wanted.
entries.description: Floating circular expanding menu with staggered item reveal.

entries.name: Card Nav
entries.lite_reason: Height/transform transition of a header panel; no forbidden features (an original should animate transform, not height).
entries.touch_reason: A tap on the toggle expands the panels; links are ordinary buttons.
entries.when: A header that expands into card panels of grouped links; rarely needed inside Messages, where one screen and header.bar carry navigation, build as a plain disclosure if a landing needs it.
entries.notes: A website nav pattern; mini-apps are one screen with header.bar and .navlink from shell.css. If a landing needs grouped section links, a disclosure of Air .panel cards under the header covers it without GSAP. The React Bits version animates height, which the doctrine forbids; use transform/opacity.
entries.description: Expandable navigation bar with card panels revealing nested links.

entries.name: Card Swap
entries.lite_reason: 3D-offset cards animated with transforms; no forbidden features.
entries.touch_reason: Cycles on a timer; a tap can advance it. No pointer needed.
entries.when: A small stack of cards where the front card drops to the back on a timer; a testimonial or feature rotator for a landing, paused to the front card under reduced motion.
entries.notes: React Bits drives it with a GSAP timeline; an original is a 3-card stack with CSS transforms and a JS interval that rotates z-order, ~1 KiB. Loop is decoration, so mark it aria-hidden or make it finite, and expose the cards' content as a list for reduced motion. This is the screen's one hero motion. fancy/stacking-cards is the scroll variant and fancy/simple-carousel the swipe variant.
entries.description: Cards animate position swapping with smooth layout transitions.

entries.name: Carousel
entries.lite_reason: Translated DOM track with drag gestures; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: Description names touch gestures; swipe is the primary input.
entries.when: Swipeable carousel with loop and snap; fancy/simple-carousel is the gallery default and already covers it.
entries.notes: Direct overlap with fancy/simple-carousel (1.4 KiB, scroll-snap, swipe). The React Bits version depends on framer-motion drag and auto-play; if looping is required, extend simple-carousel rather than vendoring.
entries.description: Responsive carousel with touch gestures, looping and transitions.

entries.name: Chroma Grid
entries.lite_reason: The grayscale veil is a full-grid overlay using backdrop-filter with a radial mask that tracks the pointer; backdrop-filter is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Colors are revealed only under a cursor spotlight; a finger has no hover position, so the grid stays gray.
entries.when: Grayscale tiles that regain color under a cursor spotlight; not for a mini-app, hover never reveals and the backdrop-filter overlay is non-lite, use an Air .grid of .tile.
entries.notes: Rules broken: hover-only reveal and cursor-following spotlight (touch first), backdrop-filter (lite). The underlying responsive card grid is just shell.css .grid/.tile with bundled images and needs no component.
entries.description: A responsive grid of grayscale tiles. Hovering the grid reaveals their colors.

entries.name: Circular Gallery
entries.lite_reason: Images are textures on bent WebGL planes rendered with OGL; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Drag spins the ring; wheel is a desktop extra.
entries.when: WebGL ring of bent images you drag to spin; a gallery on a phone uses fancy/simple-carousel, since lite forbids WebGL and the fallback is the carousel anyway.
entries.notes: Not a pack candidate: every lite/reduced-motion/no-WebGL surface needs a DOM carousel fallback, so the fallback is the component. For an orbit look, fancy/circling-elements or a CSS 3D ring (rotateY per card) is the original path. Captions are drawn on a canvas with a font name prop; keep it a system or bundled font, never a web font. Images must be bundled.
entries.description: Circular orbit gallery rotating images.

entries.name: Counter
entries.lite_reason: Digit columns translated with springs; no forbidden features.
entries.touch_reason: Animates on value change; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Digits that roll to a value with easing; fancy/basic-number-ticker already counts RSVP totals, prices and countdowns.
entries.notes: fancy/basic-number-ticker (0.7 KiB) covers count-up and countdown. The React Bits version adds odometer-style rolling digit columns via framer-motion springs; if that look is wanted it is a small CSS transform per digit, not a vendoring case.
entries.description: Flexible animated counter supporting increments + easing.

entries.name: Curved Input
entries.lite_reason: SVG textPath mirroring a hidden input; no forbidden rendering features.
entries.touch_reason: Tapping the arc focuses the hidden input, but caret, selection and autocorrect behave oddly on iOS.
entries.when: An input bent along an arc with a fake caret; not for a mini-app, inputs stay native 16px controls, and decorative arc text is fancy/text-along-path.
entries.notes: Rule broken: the doctrine wants native 16px inputs with 44px targets; this hides the real input behind an SVG mirror, so iOS selection, caret, autocorrect and zoom behave wrong, and the arc is a gimmick at 390px. Composers are aicss/agent-input or beautiful/chat-composer; a curved decorative headline is fancy/text-along-path.
entries.description: Arc-bent input bar with text, caret and submit button all following the curve.

entries.name: Decay Card
entries.lite_reason: SVG feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap on an image plus DOM transforms; not in the lite-forbidden list, though the continuous filter is costly.
entries.touch_reason: Parallax and disintegration are driven by pointer movement over the card; nothing happens under a finger.
entries.when: A card whose image displaces and dissolves as the pointer moves; not for a mini-app, there is no cursor to drive it and hover never carries meaning.
entries.notes: Rule broken: cursor-following parallax (touch first; hover may enhance, never reveal). If a pointer/orientation-reactive card is wanted, arlan/holo already tilts with device orientation. A one-shot dissolve on tap could be an original SVG displacement, but nothing here asks for it.
entries.description: Hover parallax effect that disintegrates the content of a card.

entries.name: Depth Carousel
entries.lite_reason: CSS perspective and translateZ on card elements; no WebGL or backdrop-filter implied.
entries.touch_reason: Description names drag alongside keyboard and auto-advance.
entries.when: Coverflow-style rail where cards recede into perspective as you drag; build with CSS 3D on top of simple-carousel's snap when a product spread needs depth.
entries.notes: Start from fancy/simple-carousel and add perspective, per-slot rotateY/translateZ and opacity; no library needed. Auto-advance must stop under reduced motion and swaps happen without transition. Keep the active card at 44px targets and full width at 390px.
entries.description: Cards recede into depth on a 3D rail, with drag, keyboard and auto-advance.

entries.name: Dock
entries.lite_reason: Scale transforms on icon buttons; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: Magnification is a function of cursor proximity; a finger has no proximity, so icons never scale.
entries.when: Icon bar that magnifies items near the cursor; not for a mini-app, proximity scaling has no touch equivalent and it recreates Apple's dock, use a 44px tab row.
entries.notes: Rules broken: cursor-proximity effect (touch first) and trade dress (macOS dock magnification). A bottom action row of 44px buttons from shell.css .row.actions is the Air pattern; a tap-scale of 1.05 on :active is the only motion that makes sense on a phone.
entries.description: macOS style magnifying dock with proximity scaling of icons.

entries.name: Dome Gallery
entries.lite_reason: Full-viewport scene of dozens of 3D-transformed image tiles plus a blurred enlarge overlay; too much for a DPR-1 390x360 compact card and it is not a pure CSS gradient background.
entries.touch_reason: Drag rotates the dome and tap enlarges a tile; no hover or cursor dependency.
entries.when: Photos wrapped on a draggable 3D dome as a full-screen showpiece; on a 390px card use the gallery recipe's simple-carousel, or css-box for six faces.
entries.notes: CSS 3D (rotateX/rotateY/translateZ) tiles on a sphere with drag inertia and a tap-to-enlarge overlay; no WebGL. It wants the whole viewport and dozens of images, so it fights the compact card and the one-hero rule. The gallery recipe default is fancy/simple-carousel; fancy/css-box gives a six-face 3D gallery if the 3D flavor matters. Images are owner content shipped from public/, never from a host; that is a bundle note, not a CSP risk.
entries.description: Immersive 3D dome gallery projecting images on a hemispheric surface.

entries.name: Drift Wall
entries.lite_reason: An endless full-bleed animated wall of perspective tiles is an animated background, non-lite by the Kit's background rule; only pure CSS gradient backgrounds pass lite.
entries.touch_reason: The drift is autonomous; the hover lift is an enhancement that touch loses without hiding anything.
entries.when: An endless perspective wall of tiles drifting past as ambient decor behind a hero; the Kit's simple-marquee tilted with a CSS perspective does the same job.
entries.notes: Autonomous CSS 3D loop of tiles; hover lift is decorative only, which is exactly what the touch-first rule allows. fancy/simple-marquee (pauses on reduced motion) wrapped in a perspective transform covers the effect and stays under 2 KiB. Tile images are owner content from public/, shipped in the bundle. Treat it as aria-hidden decoration, one per screen.
entries.description: An endless perspective wall of tiles drifting past, lifting on hover.

entries.name: Elastic Slider
entries.lite_reason: Transform and opacity on a thumb and track; no blur, no WebGL, no fixed backgrounds.
entries.touch_reason: Drag-driven slider; the stretch fires on drag past the ends and the snap on release, all touch native.
entries.when: A range slider whose thumb overshoots and springs back on release; use for one tunable value (tip, quantity, budget) where the flourish confirms the drop.
entries.notes: The 'spring physics' is a motion-library spring, not a physics engine. Build from a native input[type=range] (16px, 44px hit area) inside beautiful/fine-tune-card and add the overshoot as a transform spring on pointerup, settling within 300ms. Under reduced motion the thumb simply lands. Nearest Kit neighbor: beautiful/fine-tune-card.
entries.description: Slider handle stretches elastically then snaps with spring physics.

entries.name: Flowing Menu
entries.lite_reason: A sliding highlight is a translated element; nothing here needs blur, WebGL or a fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: As described, the indicator glides to whichever item becomes active, which a tap sets; the original's hover-entry marquee is the part touch cannot use and the contract forbids.
entries.when: A highlight that slides between tabs or menu rows as the active item changes; use for segmented controls and small nav, never as a hover reveal.
entries.notes: Per the description this is the sliding active highlight beautiful/glide-menu already provides (used inside approval-card, records-table and search). Skeptical note: React Bits' actual Flowing Menu slides a gsap marquee band in on hover-enter, which is a hover reveal and out under touch first. Only the tap-driven glide belongs in an app, and it needs no gsap.
entries.description: Liquid flowing active indicator glides between menu items.

entries.name: Fluid Glass
entries.lite_reason: Three.js transmission material refracting the scene; WebGL is forbidden under lite and the effect is the whole screen.
entries.touch_reason: The glass lens follows the pointer position; there is no cursor on touch and no tap or drag equivalent is described.
entries.when: A Three.js lens that refracts the page under a pointer-following glass blob; a desktop showpiece with no place inside a 390px lite card.
entries.notes: Rules broken: lite forbids WebGL; touch first forbids cursor-following effects; it loads GLB lens/bar/cube models (remote-model risk unless bundled) and renders page content through a Three transmission material, a heavy three + r3f + drei payload. Air's .panel with var(--blur) is the sanctioned glass in atmosphere. Nothing here is worth packing.
entries.description: Glassmorphism container with animated liquid distortion refraction.

entries.name: Flying Posters
entries.lite_reason: OGL WebGL plane strip with shader distortion; WebGL is forbidden under lite.
entries.touch_reason: Wheel and touch-drag both feed the scroll value, but the motion is scroll-driven, which the contract forbids regardless of input.
entries.when: Posters on a WebGL ribbon that spin as the page scrolls; scroll-linked motion is forbidden in the webview, so it has no mini-app use.
entries.notes: Rule broken: nothing moves on scroll inside a webview (no parallax, no scroll-linked reveals). Also non-lite (OGL WebGL). Poster images are owner content the Builder would ship from public/, which is fine and not a CSP risk. For a poster set use fancy/simple-carousel from the gallery recipe.
entries.description: 3D posters rotate on scroll infinitely.

entries.name: Folder
entries.lite_reason: Plain CSS transforms on a folder body, flap and two or three paper cards; no blur, no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Opens and closes on tap; the original's mouse-position nudge on the papers is decorative and drops cleanly on touch.
entries.when: A folder icon that opens on tap to fan out two or three cards; a playful disclosure for a small photo set or the items an agent gathered.
entries.notes: Simple enough to write under the contract: a 44px tappable folder colored with var(--accent), papers translated and rotated with transform over 300ms ease-out. Under reduced motion it opens and closes with no transition and the open state is a complete frame. Keep it to one per screen; it counts as the hero motion when it animates.
entries.description: Interactive folder opens to reveal nested content smooth motion.

entries.name: Glass Icons
entries.lite_reason: The frost is backdrop-filter blur on a front layer over a gradient back layer; backdrop-filter is forbidden under lite, so the effect as described is non-lite.
entries.touch_reason: Static icon tiles that work on tap; the hover tilt is a non-revealing enhancement.
entries.when: Frosted-glass icon tiles for a feature row or action grid; on Air use the color-depth glass material so lite surfaces get layered gradients, not blur.
entries.notes: arlan/color-depth already ships a 'glass' material among its ten layered-light CSS classes, lite-safe because it is gradients rather than backdrop-filter. Pair with lucide-react icons (the Kit's icon convention; no icon font). Drop the hover tilt under reduced motion; hover may enhance but the tile must read the same at rest.
entries.description: Icon set styled with frosted glass blur.

entries.name: Glass Surface
entries.lite_reason: Built on backdrop-filter (plus an inline SVG feDisplacementMap through backdrop-filter: url()), which lite forbids; only the flat fallback is lite-safe.
entries.touch_reason: A static container surface; nothing is driven by hover or pointer position.
entries.when: A refractive glass panel with edge lighting; Air's .panel with var(--blur) is the glass in atmosphere, and pixel or lite render it flat.
entries.notes: Air's atmosphere theme defines glass as data (var(--blur), var(--panel-bg), var(--ring) on .panel); pixel theme and data-lite=1 already flatten it, which is the exact degradation this component would need. The SVG displacement refraction only Chromium honors (Safari and Firefox fall back to plain blur), so it is not worth carrying. Not a trade-dress problem, just redundant.
entries.description: Advanced Apple-style glass surface with real-time distortion + lighting.

entries.name: Gooey Nav
entries.lite_reason: DOM thumb and particle spans under a blur+contrast goo filter on the element itself, not a backdrop; no WebGL, no fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Click or tap moves the active item; the goo transition follows the tap.
entries.when: A tab thumb that stretches like liquid and splits into droplets as it moves to the tapped item; use liquid-gooey, one nav per screen.
entries.notes: libraries/liquid-gooey already does the trailing tab thumb and droplet split; fancy/gooey-svg-filter is the lighter filter-only helper when that package is too heavy. A gooey nav is the screen's hero motion, so nothing else animates beside it. Reduced motion: the thumb jumps to the tapped item with no droplets.
entries.description: Navigation indicator morphs with gooey blob transitions between items.

entries.name: Infinite Menu
entries.lite_reason: React Bits' Infinite Menu is a custom-WebGL sphere of image tiles; WebGL is forbidden under lite and the scene fills the card.
entries.touch_reason: Drag or swipe spins the menu; no hover or cursor dependency.
entries.when: A menu of items that wraps endlessly as you drag or swipe; on a phone a snap carousel or a wrapping chip row covers it without the WebGL sphere.
entries.notes: The catalog line undersells it: the real component is a drag-to-spin WebGL sphere of image tiles (raw GL + gl-matrix), heavy and non-lite, with tile images the Builder would ship from public/ (owner content, not a CSP risk). An endlessly wrapping menu on a 390px screen is fancy/simple-carousel with wrap-around, or fancy/simple-marquee if it should drift on its own. Not a pack candidate: a menu never needs a shader.
entries.description: Horizontally looping menu effect that scrolls endlessly with seamless wrap.

entries.name: Infinite Spiral
entries.lite_reason: A full-screen, endlessly looping 3D scene of image tiles (CSS 3D or Three, either way heavy) is a non-lite hero; it cannot fit a 390x360 DPR-1 card.
entries.touch_reason: Described interaction is drag or swipe on the helix itself; nothing depends on hover or cursor position.
entries.when: Images on an endlessly turning 3D helix as a hero gallery; heavy, non-lite, and covered on a phone by simple-carousel or css-box.
entries.notes: Implementation uncertain: the 'depth' and 'spacing' props read like CSS perspective/translateZ, but it may be a Three scene; the verdict is the same either way. It is a full-screen 3D image scene that fights the compact card, the single column and the one-hero rule. For a photo hero use fancy/simple-carousel (gallery recipe) or fancy/css-box; images are owner content shipped from public/. Not worth packing: a helix of tiles needs no shader or physics.
entries.description: An endlessly looping 3D helix of images with customizable motion, depth, spacing and interaction.

entries.name: Lanyard
entries.lite_reason: Three.js scene with a rapier physics rope; WebGL is forbidden under lite and the card would have nothing to show.
entries.touch_reason: Grab-and-swing works through r3f pointer events on touch; the payload, not the input, is the problem.
entries.when: A badge card swinging on a physics-simulated lanyard; three, rapier and GLB assets make it a desktop showcase, not a Messages card.
entries.notes: Rules broken: it is a 3D model viewer needing a card GLB (remote-model unless bundled; the strap texture is a shipped asset, not a risk), it needs a physics engine (rapier) whose wasm requires wasm-unsafe-eval that the no-eval ceiling does not grant, and WebGL is non-lite. Exclusions already rule out physics beyond elastic-line. An event pass in a mini-app is a static .card, with arlan/holo if it should tilt with device orientation.
entries.description: Swinging 3D lanyard / badge card with realistic inertial motion.

entries.name: Line Sidebar
entries.lite_reason: Transformed list rows; no blur, WebGL or fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: The whole effect is cursor proximity shifting and highlighting nearby rows; there is no cursor on touch and no tap or drag equivalent.
entries.when: A sidebar list whose items shift toward the cursor; there is no cursor in Messages and no sidebar in a single column, so skip it.
entries.notes: Rules broken: touch first (a cursor-following effect with no touch equivalent) and the Messages layout (single column ≤ 36rem has no sidebar). Section navigation in a mini-app is header .navlink rows or beautiful/glide-menu.
entries.description: Static list navigation with a cursor-proximity effect that shifts and highlights nearby items.

entries.name: Magic Bento
entries.lite_reason: Grid of tiles with box-shadow glow and small particle spans; no backdrop-filter or WebGL, and the library already disables the effects on mobile.
entries.touch_reason: Spotlight, border glow, tilt and magnetism all follow the pointer position; only the tap ripple and a tap-to-expand survive on touch.
entries.when: A bento grid of tiles with tap-to-expand; build it from Air's .grid and .tile and drop the cursor spotlight, glow and magnetism that need a mouse.
entries.notes: React Bits' version is a gsap grid whose signature effects (cursor spotlight, border glow, particles, tilt, magnetism) are pointer-position driven and switched off on mobile by the library itself, so nothing vendored survives a phone. The layout is Air's .grid/.tile vocabulary; add a tap-to-expand tile via transform/opacity in ≤ 300ms and use libraries/border-beam on the one tile that deserves attention. Reduced motion: a static grid, which is a complete frame.
entries.description: Interactive bento grid tiles expand + animate with various options.

entries.name: Masonry
entries.lite_reason: DOM tiles positioned with transforms; no backdrop-filter, no WebGL. Only cost is layout measurement and one entrance animation.
entries.touch_reason: A static grid of tiles; hover scale in the original is an enhancement, not a reveal.
entries.when: Two-column grid of mixed-height photo tiles that settle into place once on load; the gallery grid when images vary in shape, never a layout for text.
entries.notes: Source needs gsap for the animated reflow (heavy). An original build is CSS columns or a two-column grid with an entrance transition on mount, light. At 390px cap it at two columns; the doctrine's single-column rule applies to content, a photo grid is the .grid/.tile vocabulary. Entrance runs once on mount, not on scroll into view. Tile images are the owner's, bundled from public/.
entries.description: Responsive masonry layout with animated reflow + gaps optimization.

entries.name: Model Viewer
entries.lite_reason: Three.js WebGL scene with lighting presets; WebGL is forbidden under lite and DPR 1 would make it look bad anyway.
entries.touch_reason: Orbit controls take one-finger rotate and two-finger zoom, though they fight page scroll without touch-action: none.
entries.when: Orbitable Three.js viewer for a 3D model file; not for Messages, where the model is a remote asset, WebGL is off under lite and the card is 390px wide.
entries.notes: Rules broken: no host references (GLB/GLTF files are almost always remote; bundling one blows the bundle budget), WebGL non-lite, and a product spin inside a 390x360 compact card has no compact fallback. If an app truly needs a 3D object, the planned game-3d-three recipe's primitives with an in-bundle procedural mesh are the path, not a viewer component.
entries.description: Three.js model viewer with orbit controls and lighting presets.

entries.name: Morph Slider
entries.lite_reason: Displacement transition is a fragment shader over two image textures; WebGL is off under lite.
entries.touch_reason: A slider advances on tap of prev/next or on swipe; nothing depends on hover or cursor position.
entries.when: Hero image slider that melts one photo into the next through a displacement shader; one per landing or product hero, a plain crossfade or still under lite.
entries.notes: A melt/displacement between images cannot be rebuilt well without a shader, and a photo hero for a store or landing is a legitimate mini-app use, so it earns a restricted-allowlist slot. Must ship with the same fallback contract as AirMetalFx: lite, reduced motion or no WebGL renders the current image as a still with a CSS crossfade. Images come from the bundle, not a host. fancy/simple-carousel stays the gallery default; this is the one-per-screen hero variant.
entries.description: WebGL slider that melts between images with a displacement transition.

entries.name: Option Wheel
entries.lite_reason: DOM items on a curve via 3D transforms and opacity; no filters, no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Description names drag as an input alongside wheel scroll and arrow keys, so the touch path exists.
entries.when: Curved drum picker you drag to choose one value from a short list; use it when the pick is the screen's hero, otherwise reach for a native select.
entries.notes: Not scroll-linked in the doctrine sense: it consumes wheel/drag deltas as input, it does not react to page scroll position. Inside the webview the drum needs touch-action: none and a 44px row height or it fights the page scroll. Rebuild is DOM transforms plus a snap; the original's tilt-and-fade is a per-item transform from distance to the selected index. Under reduced motion show the selected value centered with neighbours faded, no spin. Pair with a hidden native select for accessibility.
entries.description: Curved option picker that spins via scroll, drag, or arrow keys, fading and tilting items away from the selection.

entries.name: Pill Nav
entries.lite_reason: Pills plus one absolutely positioned highlight moved with transform; pure DOM/CSS.
entries.touch_reason: Tap selects; the original's per-pill hover circle is decoration and not needed.
entries.when: Row of pills with a highlight that slides to the active one; the section switcher for a tool or page app with two to four sections.
entries.notes: beautiful/glide-menu is exactly the sliding-highlight mechanic and Air's .chip/.navlink give the pill chrome; no reason to vendor a gsap-driven nav. The React Bits version also carries a logo-spin and hover fills that the doctrine treats as hover enhancement only. Keep the slide at or under 300ms ease-out; under reduced motion the highlight jumps.
entries.description: Minimal pill nav with sliding active highlight + smooth easing.

entries.name: Pixel Card
entries.lite_reason: A 2D canvas of small squares over a card; fine at DPR 1, no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: The reveal is driven by hover/focus in the original and the description gives no tap or mount trigger; hover may never reveal.
entries.when: Card whose surface fills with animated pixel squares as it appears; a once-on-mount reveal for one featured card, triggered by mount or tap, never hover.
entries.notes: Simple to build original: a canvas grid of squares that fade or scale in with per-cell delay, run once on mount or on tap, then the canvas goes inert and aria-hidden. Near neighbours in the Kit are fancy/pixelate-svg-filter (image pixelation resolving on load), arlan/ghosty-reveal (mask wipe with a supplied image) and fancy/pixel-trail (pointer-lit background); none covers an expanding-cell surface reveal. Counts as the screen's one hero motion.
entries.description: Card content revealed through pixel expansion transition.

entries.name: Profile Card
entries.lite_reason: Stacked glare and foil layers use mix-blend-mode plus a backdrop-filter blur on the info bar; heavy blend modes and backdrop-filter are non-lite.
entries.touch_reason: Tilt and glare follow the hovering pointer; no device-orientation or tap path in the description.
entries.when: Portrait card with a glare that tilts in 3D; the host or artist card at the top of a landing screen, one per screen, built on holo.
entries.notes: arlan/holo already gives the tilt plus glare, tilts with device orientation on a phone (the touch path this one lacks) and is marked one-per-screen for the same blend-mode cost. Compose the portrait, name and handle inside it with Air's .card vocabulary; no need for a second tilt card. The avatar image must be bundled.
entries.description: Animated profile card glare with 3D hover effect.

entries.name: Reflective Card
entries.lite_reason: Live video texture composited with blend modes and blur for the reflection; well past the lite ceiling.
entries.touch_reason: Glare responds to cursor movement and the reflection needs a webcam; neither exists in a Messages card.
entries.when: Card that mirrors the viewer's webcam and glares with the cursor; needs camera permission and a mouse, neither of which Messages gives you.
entries.notes: Rules broken: touch first (cursor-driven glare) and it demands getUserMedia, a camera permission prompt inside an iMessage webview that is not available and would be a privacy problem even if it were. Heavy blend modes make it non-lite regardless. No still frame exists: without the cursor there is no glare and without the camera there is no reflection, so reduced motion is none rather than static. If the goal is a reflective material, arlan/color-depth (glass, metal) or libraries/metal-fx are the Kit answers.
entries.description: Card with dynamic webcam reflection and glare effects that respond to cursor movement.

entries.name: Scroll Stack
entries.lite_reason: DOM cards with transforms; the original also blurs stacked cards with filter: blur, which is costly but not backdrop-filter or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Driven by page scroll; no hover dependence.
entries.when: Cards that pin and pile up as the page scrolls; a scroll-linked landing section the Kit only allows as sticky stacking-cards, never as JS driven by scroll position.
entries.notes: The React Bits version reads scroll position (through a smooth-scroll library) and scales/blurs cards as they stack, which is exactly the 'nothing moves on scroll inside the webview' violation. fancy/stacking-cards achieves the same pile with position: sticky, no scroll-driven transforms, so it is the sanctioned equivalent; it needs at least three cards to read. Do not pack this one; the Builder never ports the scroll-progress transforms or the Lenis dependency.
entries.description: Overlapping card stack reveals on scroll with depth layering.

entries.name: Specular Button
entries.lite_reason: Shader-driven rim light on a glass surface; WebGL plus backdrop blur, both non-lite.
entries.touch_reason: The rim light follows the cursor; the autonomous sweep survives on touch but the pointer-following half does not.
entries.when: Glass button with a bright rim light sweeping its edge; the one primary action on a screen, drawn with border-beam over a color-depth glass material.
entries.notes: A rim light sweeping the edge is what libraries/border-beam does with a rotating conic gradient and a mask, and arlan/color-depth supplies the glass material, so the shader buys nothing a mini-app can show under lite. Drop the cursor-follow entirely; a 44px button gets a tap, not a hover. Keep it to the single primary action so the beam stays the screen's one hero motion.
entries.description: Glass button with a shader-driven specular rim light that sweeps around the edge and follows the cursor.

entries.name: Spotlight Card
entries.lite_reason: A radial-gradient overlay positioned by two CSS variables; trivial paint cost.
entries.touch_reason: The spotlight follows the cursor and the description offers no tap or drag equivalent; a finger cannot hover.
entries.when: Card lit by a gradient spotlight under the cursor; there is no cursor in Messages, and a still highlight is a two-line CSS glow the Builder writes inline.
entries.notes: Rule broken: touch first, the entire effect is cursor-following. What remains without a cursor is a fixed radial highlight on a .card, which needs no component: a background-image radial-gradient on var(--panel-bg) using var(--accent) at low alpha. If an app wants attention on one card, libraries/border-beam is the Kit's answer.
entries.description: Dynamic spotlight follows cursor casting gradient illumination.

entries.name: Stack
entries.lite_reason: A few absolutely positioned cards moved with transform and opacity; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Swipe is the primary gesture; tap-to-advance and autoplay cover the rest.
entries.when: Deck of cards you swipe to send the top one to the back; a gallery or guest-photo hero when a flat horizontal carousel is not enough.
entries.notes: Straightforward to build original with pointer events and transforms: three to five cards offset by a few px and a slight rotation, drag the top past a threshold to fling it to the back. Set touch-action: pan-y so vertical page scroll survives; autoplay must be finite or aria-hidden per the motion rule. fancy/simple-carousel remains the gallery recipe default, fancy/stacking-cards is the scroll variant, this is the swipe-deck variant. Under reduced motion the swipe reorders with no fling.
entries.description: Layered stack with swipe animations, autoplay and smooth transitions.

entries.name: Staggered Menu
entries.lite_reason: Overlay panel with items translating in; transform and opacity only.
entries.touch_reason: Opens from a tap on a toggle; items are tappable rows.
entries.when: Overlay menu whose items slide in one after another on open; the nav for a multi-section page or tool app, opened from the header bar.
entries.notes: The stagger is animation-delay per row on a transform/opacity keyframe; no library needed, and the whole open must settle in about 300ms so the last row is not still arriving. Rows are 44px, the panel respects env(safe-area-inset-*), and the toggle lives in header.bar. Most mini-apps are one screen and do not need a menu at all; reach for it only when the page template has real sections.
entries.description: Menu with staggered item animations and smooth transitions on open/close.

entries.name: Stepper
entries.lite_reason: Indicator dots plus a step panel that slides; DOM transforms only.
entries.touch_reason: Next/back buttons and tappable step dots; no hover dependence.
entries.when: Multi-step form with a progress indicator and animated step changes; use it for RSVP, checkout and any form longer than one compact card.
entries.notes: A wizard is ordinary DOM: a row of dots (done/active/pending, the same states as aicss/todo-list) and one visible step panel with a ≤300ms slide between steps. Keep to four steps at 390px, 16px inputs so iOS does not zoom, 44px buttons, and write progress through useAirState so a guest sees the read-only state. Under reduced motion the panel swaps without sliding.
entries.description: Animated multi-step progress indicator with active state transitions.

entries.name: Tilted Card
entries.lite_reason: A single element with a spring-driven perspective transform; no filters or blend modes required.
entries.touch_reason: Tilt reacts to pointer position over the card; a finger drag would fight page scroll and the description gives no orientation fallback.
entries.when: Card that tilts in perspective toward the pointer; on a phone use holo, which tilts with device orientation and adds the foil only if you want it.
entries.notes: arlan/holo covers the tilt and is the Kit's one tilt card, with device orientation as the touch path this one lacks; its holographic layers can be left off for a plain tilt. One tilt card per screen and the image must come from the bundle. No reason to vendor a second pointer-driven tilt.
entries.description: 3D perspective tilt card reacting to pointer.

entries.name: ASCII Text
entries.lite_reason: Three scene with a wave shader and an ASCII post-pass; WebGL is forbidden under lite and there is no flat fallback described.
entries.touch_reason: The wave animation runs on its own; the pointer tilt only enhances and is lost without harm on touch.
entries.when: Hero word drawn as animated ASCII glyphs for a retro terminal feel; a game or lo-fi title, one per screen, using the bundled monospace, still glyphs under reduced motion.
entries.notes: The vendored version drags in Three for one word. An original: draw the word to an offscreen 2D canvas, sample luminance per cell, map to a glyph ramp, offset with a sine wave. Lite and light. Best fit is the game-2d template; a landing hero only when the whole app is retro-themed. Glyphs must come from the bundled monospace (var(--font-ui)) or system mono; no hosted font. Keep the real word in the DOM and the glyph canvas aria-hidden.
entries.description: Renders text with an animated ASCII background for a retro feel.

entries.name: Blur Text
entries.lite_reason: A filter: blur() on a few word spans with transform/opacity; no backdrop-filter, no fixed background.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous one-shot reveal on mount or on view; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Headline or confirmation line that resolves from soft blur to crisp, word by word; a one-shot mount reveal for the hero, never for body copy.
entries.notes: Two keyframes per word (blur+translateY to none) with a stagger; the Kit has no blur reveal, nearest is fancy/vertical-cut-reveal. Keep it to one line of words; blurring many glyphs is costly on a phone GPU.
entries.description: Text starts blurred then crisply resolves for a soft-focus reveal effect.

entries.name: Circular Text
entries.lite_reason: Per-character spans rotated with transform; a single slow rotation loop.
entries.touch_reason: Spins on its own; the hover speed change is an enhancement only.
entries.when: Short label set around a circle with a slow spin; a decorative badge or stamp beside a hero. Already fancy/text-along-path.
entries.notes: fancy/text-along-path sets text on an SVG circle or arc and animates along it; it also kerns correctly where per-span rotation does not. Decorative header only, aria-hidden loop.
entries.description: Layouts characters around a circle with optional rotation animation.

entries.name: Count Up
entries.lite_reason: Text node updated from a spring; nothing GPU-bound.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous count on mount or on view.
entries.when: A number that counts to its value with formatting and decimals: totals, prices, guest counts. Already fancy/basic-number-ticker.
entries.notes: fancy/basic-number-ticker is the Kit's count-up; pair with Intl.NumberFormat for separators and decimals rather than importing a second ticker.
entries.description: Animated number counter supporting formatting and decimals.

entries.name: Curved Loop
entries.lite_reason: SVG textPath with an animated startOffset; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Loops on its own and the drag interaction works with a finger.
entries.when: Phrase that loops along an SVG curve and can be dragged; a decorative band under a hero. fancy/text-along-path plus fancy/simple-marquee cover it.
entries.notes: fancy/text-along-path already animates text along an SVG path; the drag-to-scrub is a small addition if wanted. Decorative only, aria-hidden, pauses under reduced motion like simple-marquee.
entries.description: Flowing looping text path along a customizable curve with drag interaction.

entries.name: Decrypted Text
entries.lite_reason: Text content swapped per tick; no GPU work.
entries.touch_reason: Mount and on-view modes run without a pointer; the hover mode is the fancy/scramble-hover case and is hover-only.
entries.when: Label that cycles random glyphs before resolving to real text, once on mount or on view. Already fancy/scramble-in (fancy/scramble-hover for hover).
entries.notes: Use fancy/scramble-in for the one-shot reveal; fancy/scramble-hover exists for the hover flourish but is touch=false. Short labels only; scrambling a paragraph is noise.
entries.description: Hacker-style decryption cycling random glyphs until resolving to real text.

entries.name: Depth Text
entries.lite_reason: Layered text copies or stacked text-shadow with transforms; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: The parallax is driven by pointer position and the description gives no tap, drag or device-orientation equivalent.
entries.when: Extruded layered type whose parallax follows the pointer; there is no pointer in Messages, so write the static extrusion as text-shadow and skip the motion.
entries.notes: Rule broken: cursor-following effect with no touch equivalent (touch first; hover may enhance, never carry the effect). The static extruded look is one text-shadow declaration the Builder can write; if tilt motion is wanted, arlan/holo already handles device orientation.
entries.description: Layered extruded type with parallax that shifts against the pointer.

entries.name: Echo Text
entries.lite_reason: A few absolutely positioned copies animated with transform/opacity; nothing GPU-heavy.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous entrance on mount; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Ghosted copies converge and settle into one hero word; a single mount entrance for a title, static word under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Three or four aria-hidden copies offset by translate and faded, collapsing onto the real word in under 600ms. Counts as the screen's one hero motion; finite, not a loop.
entries.description: Ghosted copies trail behind the text and settle into a single word.

entries.name: Falling Text
entries.lite_reason: matter-js drives every letter span from a per-frame physics loop; the Kit marks physics non-lite (fancy/elastic-line). A CSS-keyframe rebuild is lite.
entries.touch_reason: The entrance is autonomous and the post-fall drag of letters works with a finger.
entries.when: Letters drop and bounce into a headline as a playful entrance for a game or party app; one per screen, letters already landed under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Exclusions already rule out matter-js components other than elastic-line. The description asks for gravity + bounce, which a per-letter translateY keyframe with a bounce easing and a stagger delivers; skip the piling and dragging. Under reduced motion the letters are already landed.
entries.description: Characters fall with gravity + bounce creating a playful entrance.

entries.name: Fold Text
entries.lite_reason: Per-line rotateX with perspective and transform-origin; transforms only.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous entrance on mount or on view.
entries.when: Lines unfold into place like creased paper; a one-shot hero entrance for a two or three line title, flat lines under reduced motion.
entries.notes: One keyframe: rotateX(-90deg) to 0 with perspective on the parent and alternating transform-origin per line, staggered. Nearest Kit relative is fancy/vertical-cut-reveal; use that when the fold is not the point.
entries.description: Lines unfold into place like creased paper opening flat.

entries.name: Fuzzy Text
entries.lite_reason: Small Canvas 2D that redraws horizontal slices of one word with random offsets; fine at DPR 1.
entries.touch_reason: Vibrates on its own; hover only raises the intensity, so touch loses nothing essential.
entries.when: Word that vibrates with a fuzzy edge on a small canvas; decorative game title or lo-fi hero, aria-hidden, crisp text under reduced motion.
entries.notes: An infinite loop, so it is decoration only and must be aria-hidden with the real text in the DOM for accessibility. Draw the word once to an offscreen canvas and copy row slices with jitter each frame; a tap can spike intensity in place of hover.
entries.description: Vibrating fuzzy text with controllable hover intensity.

entries.name: Glitch Text
entries.lite_reason: Two pseudo-element copies with clip-path and text-shadow keyframes; no filters, no WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Runs on its own by default; the hover-only variant would be touch=false and should not be used.
entries.when: RGB-split jitter over a hero word or game title; a short finite CSS glitch, never on status or body text, still under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Pure CSS in under 1 KB. Keep the loop finite (a burst every few seconds, or once on mount) and aria-hidden; a continuous glitch on a 390px card reads as a broken screen.
entries.description: RGB split and distortion glitch effect with jitter effects.

entries.name: Gradient Text
entries.lite_reason: background-clip: text with an animated background-position; a single composited layer.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous sweep; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Headline with a colour gradient sweeping across the glyphs; one hero word or CTA per screen, gradient held still under reduced motion.
entries.notes: A few lines of CSS using var(--accent) stops so it survives both themes. beautiful/shimmer already covers the grey loading-sweep case; this is the coloured headline case. Loop is aria-hidden decoration.
entries.description: Animated gradient sweep across live text with speed and color control.

entries.name: Masked Heading
entries.lite_reason: background-clip: text over a CSS gradient is lite; drop the drifting blurred mesh under lite and show a flat gradient, as fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg does.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous word-by-word reveal on mount or on view.
entries.when: Large headline with a drifting gradient (or bundled image) showing through the glyphs, revealed word by word; a landing hero, flat gradient under lite or reduced motion.
entries.notes: Compose from Kit parts: fancy/animated-gradient-with-svg behind, background-clip text, fancy/vertical-cut-reveal for the word stagger. The image variant is fine when the owner supplies the image from public/ inside the bundle; a remote URL prop is a CSP rejection, so the Builder must not accept one. One display size per screen.
entries.description: A large headline with a drifting colour mesh or image showing through the glyphs, revealed word by word.

entries.name: Particle Text
entries.lite_reason: Canvas 2D particle field at DPR 1 with the count capped (about 1500 for a 390px word); no WebGL, no filters.
entries.touch_reason: Scatter and reform on demand maps directly to a tap; the assembly runs on its own.
entries.when: Hero word that assembles from drifting particles and scatters again on tap; a Canvas 2D moment for a reveal or game title, assembled text under reduced motion.
entries.notes: Sample glyph pixels from an offscreen canvas into target points and ease particles toward them; a few KB, no engine. Keep the real word in the DOM (aria) and the canvas aria-hidden. If the vendored one turns out to be WebGL it is still not worth packing for a phone card.
entries.description: Text assembles from drifting particles that scatter and reform on demand.

entries.name: Rotating Text
entries.lite_reason: Word spans entering and leaving with transform/opacity; transforms only.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous cycle; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Slot in a headline that cycles phrases with a flip transition. Already fancy/text-rotate.
entries.notes: fancy/text-rotate is the Kit's cycling slot; a 3D flip is a transform-origin and rotateX variant of its transition, not a new component. Finite list, one per screen.
entries.description: Cycles through multiple phrases with 3D rotate / flip transitions.

entries.name: Scrambled Text
entries.lite_reason: Per-character DOM text with no filters, blend modes or WebGL; lite is not the problem, the pointer is.
entries.touch_reason: Driven entirely by cursor proximity; a finger over the text scrolls the card instead of hovering it, so nothing ever fires.
entries.when: Text that distorts around the cursor; there is no cursor in Messages, so skip it and unscramble a label once on mount with fancy/scramble-in.
entries.notes: Rule broken: touch first, hover may enhance but never reveal; this effect only exists under a pointer. Also drags gsap plus two plugins for a flourish the Kit already covers with a 0.8 KiB one-shot (fancy/scramble-in) and a hover-only variant (fancy/scramble-hover).
entries.description: Detects cursor position and applies a distortion effect to text.

entries.name: Scroll Float
entries.lite_reason: Transform and opacity on DOM text; no blur, fixed background or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Scroll is a touch gesture, so it technically works on a phone; it is forbidden for a different reason.
entries.when: Text that drifts and parallax-shifts as the page scrolls; nothing moves on scroll inside the webview, so give a hero a gentle idle drift with fancy/float instead.
entries.notes: Rule broken: nothing moves on scroll inside the webview, no parallax. The Messages webview scrolls the host and the card together, so scroll-linked transforms also jitter. fancy/float is time-driven and gives the same softness without the scroll dependency.
entries.description: Text gently floats / parallax shifts on scroll.

entries.name: Scroll Reveal
entries.lite_reason: Uses filter: blur() on words, which is not backdrop-filter; the pixel theme drops blur anyway, so the lite frame is just the revealed text.
entries.touch_reason: Scroll gesture only; no pointer needed, but the effect is still out.
entries.when: Words unblur and rise as they scroll into place; scroll-linked reveals are forbidden, so reveal the headline once on mount with fancy/vertical-cut-reveal.
entries.notes: Rule broken: no scroll-linked reveals; the reveal progress is scrubbed by scroll position. A one-shot in-view trigger is the Kit's accepted pattern (vertical-cut-reveal, text-highlighter), and in a 390x360 compact card the headline is already in view, so trigger on mount.
entries.description: Text gently unblurs and reveals on scroll.

entries.name: Scroll Velocity
entries.lite_reason: Transform-only marquee rows; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: Reads scroll velocity, which a finger produces; still forbidden because scroll drives the motion.
entries.when: A marquee whose speed and skew follow scroll velocity; scroll may not drive motion here, so run a constant strip with fancy/simple-marquee.
entries.notes: Rule broken: nothing moves on scroll inside the webview; the velocity coupling is the whole effect. Strip the coupling and it is fancy/simple-marquee, which already pauses under reduced motion. A full-bleed word marquee also needs two rows to read at 390px; keep it to one.
entries.description: Text marquee animatio - speed and distortion scale with user's scroll velocity.

entries.name: Shiny Text
entries.lite_reason: A gradient clipped to the text (background-clip: text) and slid with background-position; no blur, blend mode or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous loop; no pointer involved.
entries.when: A sheen that sweeps across a word or label; use it for a thinking line or one hero word, never on body copy or on more than one element per screen.
entries.notes: beautiful/shimmer is the same mechanism (gradient sweep over text) and already carries the loading semantics as the atom behind selection-actions. If the loading semantics do not fit a decorative hero word, it is ten lines of CSS built from var(--ink) and var(--accent), not a vendored file. The loop is decoration: aria-hidden or finite, frozen to one highlight position under reduced motion.
entries.description: Metallic sheen sweeps across text producing a reflective highlight.

entries.name: Shuffle
entries.lite_reason: Per-character DOM strips moved with transform; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Plays once on mount or in view; no pointer needed.
entries.when: Characters shuffle before settling into a short label; fancy/scramble-in already does this once on mount for a kicker, a price or a status word.
entries.notes: The source slides each character through a strip of copies on a gsap SplitText timeline with an in-view trigger; the Kit's scramble-in resolves random glyphs to the target in 0.8 KiB. If the slot-machine slide specifically is wanted, it is a build-original DOM strip per character with transform: translateY, not a vendored file. Keep it to short labels; a whole headline shuffling reads as noise at 390px.
entries.description: Animated text reveal where characters shuffle before settling.

entries.name: Split Flap Text
entries.lite_reason: Per-character tiles flip with rotateX transforms; no blur, blend or WebGL. Under lite drop the flip and swap glyphs.
entries.touch_reason: Runs on a timer or on data change; no pointer involved.
entries.when: A departure board that clacks through phrases tile by tile; the hero for a countdown, a guest count or an event status when fancy/text-rotate feels too soft.
entries.notes: Build it: fixed-width tiles set in var(--font-ui) (Azeret Mono is already monospace, so no board font is loaded), each tile a top and bottom half with a rotateX flip under 300ms, staggered so a phrase settles in about a second as the screen's one hero motion. Cap at roughly 12 tiles for 390px, no click audio, and under reduced motion swap glyphs instantly to the final phrase. Confidence is medium because the source's dependencies are unknown to me; the effect itself is plainly DOM/CSS.
entries.description: Mechanical split-flap departure board that clacks through to each new phrase.

entries.name: Split Text
entries.lite_reason: Transform and opacity on split spans; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: One-shot entrance; no pointer needed.
entries.when: A headline whose words or letters enter with a stagger; fancy/vertical-cut-reveal is the Kit's version, run once on mount as the screen's hero motion.
entries.notes: The source fires from a ScrollTrigger in-view threshold, which is a one-shot trigger rather than a scroll-scrubbed animation; in a 390x360 card the headline is already visible, so trigger on mount. Per-letter splitting breaks the accessible name unless an aria-label carries the full string; word-level stagger is enough at 390px and is what vertical-cut-reveal does.
entries.description: Splits text into characters / words for staggered entrance animation.

entries.name: Stroke Text
entries.lite_reason: Inline SVG text stroked with an animated dashoffset, then filled; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Plays once on mount; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Outlined letters draw themselves on and then fill; a one-shot hero for a confirmation or a launch headline on a screen with no other motion.
entries.notes: Build with inline SVG <text> in var(--font-body), stroke var(--ink), stroke-dasharray/dashoffset eased over about 1.2s, then fill-opacity 0 to 1; WebKit strokes SVG text natively. Do not outline glyphs to paths, which needs a font file (a web-font/asset risk and heavy). Under reduced motion render the filled text. One to three words at 390px so the stroke width reads; it is the screen's one hero motion. Confidence medium because I am inferring the source's renderer from the description.
entries.description: Outlined letterforms draw themselves on, then flood with fill.

entries.name: Text Cursor
entries.lite_reason: DOM copies positioned with transform; lite is fine, the pointer is not.
entries.touch_reason: Follows the cursor and spawns a trail on pointer move; a finger drag over the card fights the Messages scroll and there is no hover to trail.
entries.when: Copies of a word trail the cursor; Messages has no cursor and a drag scrolls the card, so leave it out (fancy/pixel-trail is the finger-safe trail if one is wanted).
entries.notes: Rule broken: touch first; a cursor-following effect has nothing to follow on a phone, and capturing pointermove for a trail would steal the scroll gesture. fancy/pixel-trail is the Kit's pointer/finger background and already knows to stay decorative.
entries.description: Make any text element follow your cursor, leaving a trail of copies behind it.

entries.name: Text Loop
entries.lite_reason: SVG textPath with an animated startOffset; no filters or WebGL.
entries.touch_reason: Autonomous loop; no pointer involved.
entries.when: Text that flows endlessly along a curve; fancy/text-along-path already sets a moving marquee on an SVG arc or circle for a decorative header.
entries.notes: An endless loop is decoration: aria-hidden and paused under reduced motion, as the Kit's text-along-path and simple-marquee already do. Keep the path inside the 390px column; a curve wider than the card clips and a full circle eats most of a compact card's height.
entries.description: A seamless text marquee that flows along curved SVG paths.

entries.name: Text Pressure
deps_guess: variable web font (Compressa VF or similar) loaded by URL
entries.lite_reason: font-variation-settings on per-letter spans is lite-safe in principle; the font and the pointer disqualify it, not lite.
entries.touch_reason: Warps letters by pointer distance; the only touch path is dragging across the headline, which scrolls the card instead.
entries.when: Letters swell and squeeze under the pointer through a variable font; it needs a web font and a cursor, both forbidden, so use fancy/breathing-text for an ambient word.
entries.notes: Rules broken: touch first (pointer-driven) and the CSP ceiling (the variable font is fetched from a host). The exclusions already reject variable-font components that need their own font. fancy/breathing-text does weight/width breathing on the Kit's bundled font with no pointer.
entries.description: Characters scale / warp interactively based on pointer pressure zone.

entries.name: Text Type
entries.lite_reason: Plain text nodes plus a blinking caret span; nothing lite forbids.
entries.touch_reason: Plays on mount; no pointer involved.
entries.when: A typewriter with a blinking caret and adjustable cadence; fancy/typewriter (or arlan/typer when you need the erase) is the Kit's version for a headline or status line.
entries.notes: Weight follows the rule (the source pulls gsap for a caret blink); fancy/typewriter is 0.9 KiB and arlan/typer 2.7 KiB with the out-animation. For a real agent reply use aicss/streaming-text, which reveals actual tokens, rather than faking cadence with a typewriter. Not for body copy; under reduced motion show the finished line with a static caret or none.
entries.description: Typewriter effect with blinking cursor and adjustable typing cadence.

entries.name: True Focus
entries.lite_reason: filter: blur() on unfocused words is not backdrop-filter, but the pixel/lite theme has no blur, so dim them with opacity there and keep the frame.
entries.touch_reason: Auto-cycles through the words in order on a timer; the optional hover mode is dropped.
entries.when: A focus frame steps across a short phrase, sharpening one word at a time; a finite hero for a three or four word promise on a landing screen, never for copy people must read.
entries.notes: Build it: one span per word, the active word filter: none and the rest blur(4px) (opacity .5 under lite/pixel), four corner brackets moved between word rects with transform, roughly 700ms per step, finishing parked on the last word so the loop is finite. Under reduced motion every word is sharp and the frame sits on the first word. Weight rates the source (framer-motion); the original build is well under 2 KiB. Not equivalent to fancy/text-rotate, which swaps words rather than focusing them.
entries.description: Applies dynamic blur / clarity based over a series of words in order.

entries.name: Variable Proximity
deps_guess: variable web font (Roboto Flex or similar) from Google Fonts
entries.lite_reason: Per-letter font-variation-settings is lite-safe; the pointer and the hosted font are the problem.
entries.touch_reason: Continuously maps pointer distance to letter weight and width; no hover exists on a phone and a drag scrolls the card.
entries.when: Letter weight and width bend toward the pointer through a variable font; no cursor in Messages and no web fonts under the CSP, so use fancy/breathing-text for an ambient word.
entries.notes: Rules broken: touch first (cursor-following) and the CSP ceiling (a Google Fonts variable font). Same family as text-pressure; the Kit's answer to variable-axis text is fancy/breathing-text on the bundled font, ambient and pointer-free.
entries.description: Letter styling changes continuously with pointer distance mapping.

entries.name: Warp Text
entries.lite_reason: A WebGL shader pass over the text; lite forbids WebGL and the Kit's only WebGL exception is libraries/metal-fx, which falls back to a flat plate.
entries.touch_reason: The refraction follows the pointer; on a phone nothing happens unless a finger drags across it, which fights the scroll.
entries.when: A WebGL pass bends and refracts a headline around the pointer; cursor-driven and non-lite, so leave it out; libraries/metal-fx is the one WebGL hero treatment the Kit allows.
entries.notes: Rules broken: touch first (cursor-following) and WebGL under lite. It is not a Tier B pack candidate either: strip the pointer and it renders plain text, so there is nothing to degrade to that is not already just the headline. If the text is drawn from an MSDF atlas the source also carries a font asset, which I cannot confirm from the description.
entries.description: WebGL warp that bends and refracts the text around the pointer.

corrections.reason: fancy/css-box is already a CSS 3D cube in the Kit; a rotating cluster is a grid of css-box instances on one keyframe, so nothing new needs building (failure mode 4).
Name the Tier A component that covers the effect; the annotator's own notes already pointed at it.

corrections.from: A small cluster of CSS cubes turning slowly as a hero object; one per screen, auto-rotating, with hover as an optional extra, never the only input.
corrections.to: A small cluster of CSS cubes turning slowly as a hero object; compose it from fancy/css-box, auto-rotating, with hover as an optional extra and never the only input.
corrections.reason: When-line must point at the Kit equivalent now that the disposition is kit-a-equivalent.

The description gives 'click pulses' (a tap equivalent) and a finger drag supplies the pointer position exactly as it does for fancy/pixel-trail, which the Kit marks touch=true; marking the same idea touch=false while naming pixel-trail as its equivalent is inconsistent.

corrections.from: Cells light up around a hovering cursor; on a phone the grid sits dark until a finger drags, and only the click pulse maps to tap.
corrections.to: Click pulses map to tap and a finger drag supplies the pointer position, so cells light under the finger the same way fancy/pixel-trail does; the hover falloff at rest is the only part lost.
corrections.reason: Reason must match the corrected touch verdict.

corrections.from: A canvas grid whose cells glow around the pointer and pulse on click; the Kit's pixel-trail already does the finger-driven version, so use that.
corrections.to: A canvas grid whose cells glow under the pointer or finger and pulse on tap; the Kit's pixel-trail already does this, so use that.
corrections.reason: Align the when-line with touch=true and the tap equivalent.
